### 19.107 Runtime COS surface discovery and the protocol-conformance gap (2026-11-01)

- **Repository identity:** the generation/Runtime repository is `C:\AI` (remote `github.com/dio16/ai-generation-loop-orchestrator`), clean at `f9867478`. This matches the Runtime inspection recorded in §19.40-era evidence.
- **What exists:** a FastAPI application (`orchestrator_app/api.py`) exposes a COS-shaped surface under `/api/cos`: `catalog`, `tasks` (create/page/view), `tasks/{id}/candidates` and candidate detail, `evaluations/{candidate}`, `history`, `details`, `commands/{command_id}`, `tasks/{id}/stop`, and `media/{digest}` descriptor/blob/thumbnail, with auth (`/api/auth/*`) and CSRF endpoints. Payloads are Pydantic models with `extra="forbid"`.
- **Why MP-RT1 cannot start yet:** the Runtime payloads do not carry the Desktop protocol's identity and revision fields. `TaskViewPayload` has `task_id`, `task_status`, `phase`, `iteration`, `watch`, `accepted_input`, `outcome`, `available_actions`, `issues`, but no epoch, projection revision, capabilities reference, graph revision, formal outcome reference or iteration entity identity that `desktop-protocol::TaskSnapshot` requires. Candidate, evaluation, history and media payloads show the same class of gap. A Desktop-side mapping cannot invent those values, and the Desktop may not derive canonical state locally.
- **Required Runtime work (next task, separate repository):** expose protocol-conformant read projections and command receipts — epoch/session identity, projection revision, capabilities reference, iteration entities, graph revision identity, formal outcome references, stop/command receipts with dedupe — or publish a documented mapping that the Desktop adapter can verify. Until that exists, MP-RT1–RT8, SEC1, ACC1/ACC2, IMG6 and INS2 stay `RUNTIME_BLOCKED`; the `/api/cos` surface is evidence that the target exists, not that it is compatible.
- **Desktop-side preparation that is already valid:** the bounded decoder (§19.106), the fixture/public-seam client, the protocol DTOs and the transport-independent client boundary. No Desktop source was changed for this survey; it is documentation-only (Y04), with no Gate and no Runtime or product acceptance claim.

### 19.108 Runtime projection and the Desktop REST read adapter (2026-11-01)

- **Runtime change (separate repository, `dio16/ai-generation-loop-orchestrator` `dev`):** `33ba9770` adds the Desktop read-projection wire contract to `contract-core` (`TaskViewV1`, `IterationViewV1`, `CandidateRefViewV1`, `GraphRefViewV1`, `CommandReceiptV1`, `StopAckV1`; deny-unknown-field deserialization, schema_version 1, reference validation). `6d73541c` makes `GET /api/cos/tasks/{task_id}` emit `epoch`, `projection_revision`, `title`, `capabilities_ref` (the recorded capability snapshot-set digest of the latest run) and `stop_pending`. Iteration, graph revision and formal outcome stay absent because the Runtime has no recorded row to source them from; the projection never fabricates them. Verified there with `cargo test -p contract-core` (all pass), clippy `-D warnings`, and `pytest tests/test_cos_frontend_contract.py` (64 passed) plus an ASGI `/api/ready` 200 check.
- **Desktop adapter:** `cos-client::runtime_http` reads `/api/cos/tasks/{task_id}` through an injected `HttpExecutor` and enforces the epoch/revision guards: the epoch is required, a revision inside one epoch may only move forward (`RevisionRegression` refuses a regression and keeps the last accepted revision), a new epoch resets the baseline, a payload for another task, an empty axis, a non-200 status or a malformed body are refused, and task ids are percent-encoded so they cannot add path structure. The crate keeps no network dependency; a concrete executor belongs to the binary/startup boundary.
- **Golden payload:** `crates/cos-client/fixtures/runtime-task-view-v1.json` is generated from the Runtime's own Pydantic projection (not hand-written). Drift is caught by regenerating and diffing; the saved copy alone cannot detect a later Runtime change, which the fixture README states.
- **Not claimed:** this is a read adapter, not the full `Transport`: the Desktop byte-frame protocol (snapshot begin/chunk/end, delta transactions, receipts) is not yet derived from the REST payload, so MP-RT1 stays open for observation/command wiring, and no product surface consumes it yet.
- **Review round 2 (2026-11-01):** the adapter now requires `stop_pending` instead of defaulting it to `false` (a missing Stop fact no longer reads as "not stopping"), refuses a task id that is exactly `.` or `..` before any HTTP call, and applies the Runtime's reference bounds (512 bytes / 1024 title bytes, no control characters). The Runtime model makes `stop_pending` required in `7b35c935`. Fixture provenance (generation command, Runtime commits, regeneration rule) is recorded in `crates/cos-client/fixtures/README.md`.
- **Review round 3 (2026-11-01):** the fixture README now carries a runnable regeneration command (verified byte-identical against the runtime model) and states that a saved fixture cannot detect later drift on its own; the phase bound matches the Runtime's 64-**character** limit (with a 64-multi-byte-character acceptance test and a 65-character refusal test), and the fixture provenance table records `7b35c935`.
- **Review round 4 (2026-11-01):** the fixture README names the full path into this checkout for the redirect (the Runtime working directory has no such relative path) and its introduction no longer claims that a saved fixture detects drift; the Runtime's Rust wire contract makes `stop_pending` required in `7ebd4098` with a rejection test, so Pydantic, Rust and the Desktop adapter agree.
- **External review (rounds 1–4, CLEAN):** round 1 found a defaulted `stop_pending` and an ambiguous `.`/`..` task id; round 2 found a non-runnable fixture recipe and a phase bound that did not match the runtime; round 3 found a stale drift-detection claim and a leftover `serde(default)` in the Runtime contract; round 4 returned `PASS 0 / 0 / 0, VERDICT: CLEAN` on `77dd929df6cf9403f088c1217c28a3c982043c30`. The reviewer kept the byte-frame gateway, the real HTTP executor, authentication and product integration out of scope, so MP-RT1 stays open.

### 19.109 Why the byte-frame transport cannot be synthesized on the Desktop side (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** `desktop-protocol::SnapshotEnd` declares `scope`, `epoch`, `cursor`, `expected: SnapshotCounts` and `integrity_digest` "over the canonical encoding of all staged mutations", and `SnapshotChunk` carries `Upsert { base_revision, projection }`. `OpenAuthorizedObservation` requires a bounded read grant (`ReadGrant`) with the exact binding, and `ClientMessage` has no REST-shaped request.
- **Consequence:** a Desktop-side HTTP adapter that turned `/api/cos/tasks/{id}` into `SnapshotBegin/Chunk/End` would have to mint the read grant, the cursor, the expected counts and the snapshot integrity digest itself. Those are server statements the client verifies for completeness and integrity; a client that both produces and verifies them removes the guarantee. That is local canon derivation, which the product canon forbids regardless of convenience.
- **Correct owner:** the Runtime (or a Runtime-owned gateway process) must serve the Desktop protocol: grant the observation scope, emit the snapshot with a server cursor and digest, and stream deltas. The Desktop keeps `RuntimeReader` (`cos-client::runtime_http`) as the verified REST read path it already owns, and adds the protocol transport only against that server.
- **Not done, and not planned as Desktop work:** frame synthesis from REST payloads, a client-issued `ReadGrant`, or a local integrity digest. The remaining MP-RT1–RT8 chain therefore needs a Runtime-side protocol endpoint task; the Desktop side is blocked on it rather than incomplete.

### 19.110 Evaluation scores as DecimalV1 strings, and the CanonicalV1 bundle digest (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** Step 1 made `desktop-protocol::canonical_json` emit the Runtime's `CanonicalV1` (sorted NFC keys, omitted null object members, compact separators, NFC strings, Python `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False)` escaping, integers only) and added the domain-separated `projection_bundle_digest` (`sha256("desktop-projection" ‖ 0x00 ‖ canonical)` over `{"schema_version": 1, "mutations": [...]}`). The Runtime `canonical_json_v1` rejects JSON floats by type, so `EvaluationSnapshot`'s `NamedScore.value` and `confidence` (`f64`) and `ParameterValue::Decimal(f64)` made every evaluation-bearing snapshot/delta bundle undigestible: the committed fixture failed at `FixtureRuntime::snapshot_bundle()` and 66 tests failed with the client stuck in `Synchronizing`.
- **Decision:** the numeric axes are carried as Runtime-issued **DecimalV1 canonical decimal text** (`Option<String>`; `ParameterValue::Decimal(String)`). Wire field names, namespaces and meaning are unchanged. Integral values use plain integer text (`58.0` → `"58"`), fractional values keep their decimal text (`0.55` → `"0.55"`). The fixture and the ui-model inspector/tests were migrated in the same change; the numeric axis demo is preserved, not deleted.
- **Why not keep `f64`:** floats cannot be part of a canonical payload while the Runtime owns a float-free encoding, so keeping them would either break parity or force the Desktop to invent a float rule the Runtime does not share. Determinism (no NaN/`-0.0`/round-trip drift) and precision safety follow from the string form.
- **Authority and non-validation:** DecimalV1 is a Runtime format; the Desktop neither duplicates its validator nor parses the value into `f64`. It renders the string verbatim. Duplicating the validator would create a second owner for a Runtime rule and invite drift; the Runtime validates what it issues and the string is only displayed locally.
- **Known limit:** the Desktop has no numeric processing of these decimal strings yet (no local arithmetic, comparison, averaging or rounding). Any future feature that needs it requires an explicit Runtime-owned derivation, not client-side parsing.
- **Pinned by:** `desktop-protocol` canonical unit tests (sorting, null omission, NFC equivalence and key collision, escaping, float rejection, integers wider than `u64`/`i64`, U+212B/U+0958 NFC, non-BMP key order, literal domain and digest pin) and the Runtime-generated parity vectors (`desktop-projection-v1` and the shared `canonical-v1-parity` corpus, both copied unchanged from the `contract-core` CLI and never edited on the Desktop side). Command/receipt dedupe digests stay domainless (`integrity_digest_of`) and are not wire-verified bundle digests.
- **Migration boundary:** because `canonical_json` changed from `serde_json::to_vec` to CanonicalV1, the domainless `integrity_digest_of` value for a given payload also changed. That is accepted: command/receipt dedupe digests are issued and verified inside the client (fixture included), no old digest is persisted or migrated, and no command digest is wire-verified today. A future Runtime-verified command digest needs its own domain-separated spec rather than this domainless function.

### 19.111 TaskSnapshot optionality for facts the Runtime cannot project (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** the COS Runtime read model cannot supply three `TaskSnapshot` facts. `creative_tasks` has no display-id column; `inner_phase` derives from `creative_runs.phase`, so a task with no run has none; `capabilities_ref` derives from `capability_snapshot_sets`, so a task with no run has none. `TaskViewV1` (the REST read adapter in `cos-client::runtime_http`) already declares `display_id`/`phase`/`capabilities_ref` optional; the protocol DTO alone required them, so a conforming server could not state the truth.
- **Decision (schema 2.0 Draft, protocol doc owner):** `TaskSnapshot.display_id: Option<String>`, `inner_phase: Option<PhaseLabel>` and `capabilities_ref: Option<CapabilitiesId>`, each `#[serde(default)]`. Absent means "the Runtime did not project this fact"; the client never substitutes a plausible value and the canonical bundle digest omits the null member. `Candidate`, `Artifact`, `Evaluation`, `Iteration`, `Outcome`, `Graph` and `CreativeCapabilities` keep their required projections until a Runtime read-model task scopes them; this section does not pre-approve that widening.
- **Client behaviour when the fact is absent:** the task rail and dock/inspector display label falls back to the `task_ref` wire identity for display only (commands still target `task_ref`, never the label); the phase axis and rail show the existing explicit unknown marker (`不明`), not a fabricated phase; an absent `capabilities_ref` is *not projected*, so it produces no capabilities lookup and no dangling-reference attention row, and stop/command availability fails closed through the existing "操作可否の情報がありません" path. A `Some(reference)` whose projection is missing from the snapshot stays a dangling reference exactly as before.
- **Explicitly not done:** no client-side display-id derivation, no default phase, no capability synthesis, no `TaskViewV1`/Wire field rename, and no change to Candidate/Artifact/Evaluation projects.
- **Pinned by:** `desktop-protocol` serde tests (a task missing all three fields deserializes with `None`, never `""` or a phase value), `ui-model` tests (fallback label, unknown phase marker, absent-capabilities attention/lookup), and the committed fixture, which still projects all three values and therefore exercises the populated path.

### 19.112 Runtime mode reads the real Runtime through app-core (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** Step 3 delivered `cos-client::ProtocolTransport` with an injected `ProtocolHttp` executor over the Runtime REST routes (`GET /api/cos/desktop/server`, `POST /api/cos/desktop/observation`, `GET /api/cos/desktop/deltas`). Step 4 wires it into the native composition root so runtime mode reads real Runtime tasks: `apps/desktop/src/runtime.rs` resolves `COS_DESKTOP_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT`/`COS_DESKTOP_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, builds `ProtocolTransport` + `CosClient` (source `Unknown`, which the client replaces with `Runtime` after the handshake), and hands it to `window::ObservationHost` exactly like the fixture branch. The UI still reads only the app-core `ObservationHandle`; no UI layer calls `cos-client`.
- **Transport decision:** the executor uses `ureq = { version = "2.12", default-features = false }` in `apps/desktop` only — a blocking plain-HTTP client with no TLS, compression, cookie or proxy feature. The origin must be an explicit **loopback IP-literal** plain-HTTP origin (`127.0.0.0/8` or `[::1]`, port 1-65535) with no embedded credentials, no path, query or fragment; host names — `localhost` included — and every other literal are refused as an unsupported endpoint before a client exists, because a host name's resolved address can change between validation and connection (a TOCTOU the cleartext bearer and `X-Cos-Context` cannot afford) and a cleartext credential must never leave the machine. Redirects are disabled (`redirects(0)`) and environment proxies are ignored so a bearer credential can never be replayed to another origin; the whole-request timeout is 15 s and the accepted response body is bounded (staged bundle ceiling + one control frame). `ureq` is a crates.io dependency of the binary only; it adds no workspace edge and no TLS/crypto crate.
- **Token boundary:** `COS_DESKTOP_RUNTIME_TOKEN` is read once at startup, moved into the **protocol transport** (the executor holds no credential) and presented as `Authorization: Bearer …` on exactly the three protocol routes — observation open, snapshot read, delta read (RC-03; see §19.114, which supersedes the earlier POST-only rule). It is never rendered, logged, placed in diagnostics/crash reports or echoed in error messages; failures report `ureq`'s closed `ErrorKind` (which cannot contain the URL or token) instead of the underlying message. A missing endpoint, non-plain-HTTP endpoint or missing token is an explicit unavailable state: no client is built, `AppCore::disconnected(true)` renders "Disconnected — Runtime endpoint configured but not reachable or authorized", and **no fixture client is ever constructed in runtime mode**.
- **Not implemented (reported honestly):** TLS, a real authentication/principal model (the bearer token is a development credential; MP-PUB1 stays NOT_IMPLEMENTED and the `X-Cos-Context` bearer remains a capability, not a principal), command submission/stop over the REST protocol (observation only), production discovery/pairing, and any server-side session reuse/resume guarantee.
- **Pinned by:** `apps/desktop` runtime unit tests (runtime mode without endpoint/token is explicitly unavailable and never plans a fixture; non-HTTP and credential-bearing endpoints are refused without echoing them; the executor returns status+body, forwards the transport's headers and adds no credential of its own, bounds the body and never echoes the credential on transport failure), plus the Lead's live smoke against the Runtime adapter (39-task snapshot, CLI-matching digest, `deltas: null`, missing-context 401).

### 19.113 Observation v1 compatibility matrix from recorded Runtime responses (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** MP-RT1 asked both sides to pin the *actual* observation-v1 exchange, not only an agreed schema. The Runtime recorded real HTTP exchanges over a live adapter (`fixtures/desktop-observation-v1/`, Runtime commit `4b3e377d`, captured 2026-11-01T07:00:24Z against a DB copy with 39 scoped tasks: 37 with run history, 2 without) into one JSON envelope per scenario (`{name, request{method,path,headers}, response{status}, body}`): `hello`, `observation-grant`, `snapshot`, `deltas-none`, `deltas-changed`, `deltas-resync` (409), `context-missing` (401), `observation-unauthorized` (401), `version-rejected` (422 `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL`). The Desktop copies are byte-identical (`crates/cos-client/fixtures/desktop-observation-v1/`). The byte-identity pin is **LF-based** (the content git stores) and hashes CRLF→LF normalized bytes, so a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` cannot break it and no `.gitattributes` is required; the pinned values are the Runtime README's LF digests, e.g. `hello.json` `b6c9fad7…`, `observation-grant.json` `01deb64d…`, `deltas-changed.json` `324f9f7d…`.
- **Matrix:** the accepted combination (protocol/schema `2.0`/`2.0`, `GET /server` handshake, `POST /observation` with an echoed request id/scope, bearer only on the open, `X-Cos-Context` capability on reads, TASK-only snapshot with server-issued cursor/counts/digest/epoch, absent optional facts never defaulted, deltas with predecessor/epoch binding) and every rejection condition (unsupported pair, missing/unknown context, missing bearer, unknown/expired cursor, epoch change, digest/count mismatch, dangling reference, grant echo mismatch) are normative in DESKTOP_PROTOCOL.md "Observation v1 compatibility matrix". The plan does not restate them as a second contract.
- **Known-cursor 409 semantics (RC-05 A-04):** a cursor the Runtime issued is normally replayable (`200` `{"transaction": null}` or the transaction), but DESKTOP_PROTOCOL.md now records that the Runtime returns `409 RESYNC_REQUIRED` when it decides replay is unsafe: unrepresentable history (the scope's content returned to the issued revision, A→B→A), a temporary Task inserted then deleted inside the scope (`view=all`), a journal gap (retention window exceeded, pruned, or reset by an epoch initialisation), a cursor expired by the journal retention bound, or an epoch mismatch (ledger owned by another process / re-initialised by restart). That is a deliberate Runtime design decision: state "cannot replay" explicitly instead of synthesising a substitute diff. The client contract is unchanged — a 409 publishes nothing, keeps the last fully applied cursor and re-observes — and observation v1's limited implementation scope (TASK-only, no commands) is unchanged.
- **Fixture provenance (RC-03):** the frozen fixtures record the **pre-RC-03** HTTP auth contract: the recorded successful `GET`s (`snapshot`, `deltas-none`, `deltas-changed`) carry no `Authorization` header, and the current Runtime answers that request with `401`. They remain the historical record of the contract they captured and are **not evidence of the current authenticated contract**; the current authenticated exchange evidence lives in the Runtime's pytest suite (e.g. `test_desktop_reads_require_and_bind_the_credential_principal`, plus the principal/audience and resync cases) and in §19.114. The Desktop does not rewrite them: both repositories keep the identical git blobs, and the Desktop replay presents the credential via the transport as the current contract requires.
- **Evidence and replay adaptations:** `crates/cos-client/tests/observation_compat_v1.rs` drives the real `CosClient`/`ProtocolTransport` through those documents. Two session-correlation fields cannot replay verbatim and are re-echoed exactly as the server contract defines them, never fabricated into content: `grant.stamp.request_id` echoes the replayed client's request id, and the `deltas-changed` envelope's `epoch`/`predecessor` are rebound to the replayed session because that scenario was captured on a second server copy. Mutation content, `mutation_count`, `transaction_id`, successor cursor and `integrity_digest` stay recorded; the digest covers only mutations, so rebinding cannot weaken verification. `crates/cos-client/src/projection.rs` additionally validates the recorded grant snapshot through the client's own `ProjectionState::from_snapshot` entry/integrity path (counts and CanonicalV1 bundle digest reproduced).
- **Asserted outcomes:** recorded grant → `Live` with 39 tasks, server-issued cursor, validated publication (run-history and run-less tasks both accepted); recorded `null` poll → no mutation, cursor retained; recorded transaction → applied atomically, revision advances, successor cursor retained, no resync; recorded 409 → transport failure, no fabricated cursor and no mutation from the rejection body, then a second recorded `POST` re-observes to `Live`; recorded 401s → publication withheld (`AuthorizationUnavailable`), no data published, `Incompatible`/withheld fail-closed for the rejected open; recorded 422 → fail-closed `Incompatible`, no data.
- **Non-goals (unchanged):** command submission/receipts over the REST protocol, a principal authentication model (the bearer is a development credential; MP-PUB1 stays NOT_IMPLEMENTED), TLS, projection kinds other than TASK (candidate/artifact/evaluation/iteration/outcome/graph/capabilities), resume/replay guarantees for a fresh process, and any Runtime-side change.
- **Pinned by:** the nine `observation_compat_v1` tests (fixture sha256 copies, digest/count reproduction, accepted-flow replay, each recorded rejection) and the `projection::recorded_observation_v1` unit test.

### 19.114 Principal-bound reads present the Desktop credential on all protocol reads (2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** RC-03 moved read authorization from a capability-only rule to a principal-bound rule: the Runtime now requires the Desktop credential on `GET /api/cos/desktop/snapshot` and `GET /api/cos/desktop/deltas`, and binds the issued context, scope and cursor to the issuing principal. The earlier S4/RC-02 repair (B-03, §19.112) kept the bearer on the observation `POST` only *because reads were then authorized solely by `X-Cos-Context`*. That premise no longer holds, so the POST-only rule is **superseded**, not reopened: B-03's closed finding covered a stale premise, and the invariant it protected — the credential never reaches a non-protocol path or another origin — is unchanged.
- **Decision (single owner):** `ProtocolTransport` presents `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on exactly the three protocol routes (`/api/cos/desktop/observation`, `/snapshot`, `/deltas`) and on no other path; a query string belongs to the route and cannot extend the set. `ProtocolTransportConfig::bearer_token` is the only credential input. The binary's `ureq` executor is credential-free and forwards the transport's headers verbatim, so it cannot attach a credential to another path or origin; the loopback IP-literal origin restriction, disabled redirects and ignored environment proxies from §19.112 remain in force.
- **Why the transport owns it:** the transport builds every protocol request, so one place both decides which routes carry the credential and guarantees the handshake and every future non-protocol route stay clean. Keeping the token in the executor would have duplicated the rule at two layers with no path knowledge at the transport.
- **Client expectation:** a read denied for a missing, invalid or foreign credential is a transport failure: the publication is withheld (`AuthorizationUnavailable`), nothing from the response is applied, and the client re-observes; a `403 PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH` or `403 AUDIENCE_MISMATCH` is never repaired locally, and the handshake route continues to carry no credential. The status matrix (401 `{"detail"}` for the credential, 401 `UNAUTHORIZED_CONTEXT` for the context, 403 for principal/audience, 409 for cursor/epoch) is normative in DESKTOP_PROTOCOL.md.
- **Evidence:** `protocol_transport` unit and integration tests pin the route set (`is_protocol_route`, captured request headers: credential on the open and the delta read, none on the handshake; query-carrying paths still recognized), the executor test proves the binary forwards headers and adds none of its own, and the recorded-response replay presents the credential on the reads and adds a credential-less-read case that withholds the publication with no data applied. The frozen fixtures remain the **pre-RC-03** historical record and are not evidence of the current authenticated contract (§19.113 "Fixture provenance"); the current authenticated exchanges are evidenced by the Runtime pytest suite (`test_desktop_reads_require_and_bind_the_credential_principal` and the principal/audience/resync cases). The fixtures are unchanged: both repositories keep the same nine JSON files and README blob.
- **Pinned by:** `crates/cos-client` (`credential_route_tests`, `the_credential_is_presented_on_the_protocol_reads_only`), `apps/desktop` runtime tests, and `observation_compat_v1::reads_without_a_credential_withhold_the_publication`.

### 19.115 Desktop Runtime credential storage in the Windows Credential Manager (MP-SEC1, 2026-11-01)

- **Observation:** the Desktop credential (RC-03) was supplied only through `COS_DESKTOP_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, so every launch needed the environment variable and there was no protected way to keep the credential between sessions. A plain file would violate the no-plaintext rule.
- **Decision (store choice):** the Desktop stores it as a Windows Credential Manager generic credential (`CRED_TYPE_GENERIC`, machine-persistent) through the `keyring` safe wrapper (`windows-native` backend only; our own code contains no `unsafe`, and the crate adds no TLS, async or other platform store). Service (target) name = `cos-desktop/observation/<sha256(origin)[..32]>`, user name `desktop-observation`. The name is a digest so the entry cannot be located by guessing a URL, and it is stable across rotation. The entry is **origin-scoped**: v1 projects no principal identity on the wire; the Runtime still binds the issued context to its principal, and a rejected credential is revoked rather than reused. Non-Windows builds register no store and accept the environment override only.
- **Lifecycle:** startup precedence is **environment override > stored entry > explicit "credential unavailable"** (`CredentialUnavailable`, an explicit disconnected surface; no unauthenticated attempt and no fixture fallback). An environment token is used for the session and written back to the store, so a rotated credential replaces the stored value and later launches need no variable. A `401` from a **credential-bearing route only** (observation open, snapshot read, delta read) deletes the entry (at most once per session) and prints a value-free re-authorization notice; a `401` from the handshake route carries no credential and never revokes a valid entry (it surfaces as an unreachable/unauthorized endpoint instead). The client's existing rule keeps the publication withheld, so nothing from a rejected credential is shown. A store failure is never fatal when an override exists (one value-free stderr label), and a failed deletion keeps the session in the explicit re-authorization state rather than pretending success.
- **Threat model (what is protected):** the only persistence path is the OS per-user store (DPAPI-backed); no code path writes the credential to the repository tree, a preferences/settings file, a log line, a support report or a crash report, and `Debug`/store errors/transport failures are value-free by construction. The bounded-scan test below adds limited file-level evidence for the app-data and temp roots; it is not a whole-machine guarantee.
- **What is NOT protected (honest limits):** the plaintext evidence is a **bounded scan** (files ≤4 MiB under the app-data and temp roots, a capped walk, exclusions and read failures recorded), so it says nothing about very large files, unreadable files, other directories, crash dumps, shell history, other user profiles or process memory; code running as the same user can read the Credential Manager entry (the store is not an ACL against the user's own processes); an administrator or kernel-level attacker can read memory or the store; the credential still lives in process memory with no zeroization guarantee and one heap copy in the transport; it travels over plain loopback HTTP without TLS; the store protects at rest only — not a compromised session, debugger or memory dump; there is no principal identity on the wire, so the key is origin-scoped and a principal change is detected by rejection, not by key separation; there is no automatic refresh flow — rotation means the operator supplies a new credential.
- **Evidence:** `apps/desktop` Windows-native tests: Credential Manager round trip (write → read → delete, idempotent delete, unique per-test service name, drop guard cleanup), the **bounded plaintext scan** (one unique token) whose required roots are created by the test itself as two non-overlapping sibling directories next to the test binary, each holding three known probe files, so the scan depends on **no environment variable** (`LOCALAPPDATA`/`TEMP`/`TMP` may all be absent); the app-data and system-temp roots are optional, scanned only when present and recorded as `roots_absent`/`optional_roots_skipped` otherwise. Coverage is recorded **per root** by fixed label (`required-a`, `required-b`, `app-data`, `temp`; the real path is never logged): (`label`, `files_scanned`, `oversize_skipped`, `capped`, `unreadable_entries`) with independent per-directory entry and per-root file budgets, so one large root cannot consume another's budget; enumeration errors from `ReadDir`, unreadable sub-directories and unreadable entries are all counted as `unreadable_entries`, and the test asserts each required root was walked fully (`capped == false`), had no unreadable entries, and really scanned at least its probe files. A rendered support report is also checked. A separate determinism test injects an absent root to prove an absent/unreadable root is recorded and never counted as scanned. Runtime-resolution tests: environment override wins and replaces the stored value, stored credential loads when the environment is absent, missing/failing store is explicitly unavailable. Revocation tests: a `401` on each of the three credential-bearing routes revokes exactly once, a `401` on the handshake route never revokes (the stored value survives), a `200` never revokes, and a failed deletion keeps the explicit re-authorization state without a retry loop. Existing transport, observation-compat and fixture-mode tests are unchanged.
- **Non-goals:** MP-RT2 full authenticated connection, MP-SEC2 native crash verification, Runtime-side authentication/authorization changes, command/receipt delivery, TLS, service discovery, a general IAM or custom cryptography, and production authentication READY. "MP-SEC1 Desktop-limited completion" is not "MP-RT2 authenticated Runtime connection complete".

### 19.116 MP-SEC2 Desktop: limited native abnormal-exit secret-exposure verification (2026-11-01)

- **Scope:** [DC-MP-SEC2](../architecture/DESKTOP_DESIGN_CONTRACTS.md#dc-mp-sec2) and [Windows crosswalk row 12](../architecture/DESKTOP_DESIGN_CONTRACTS.md#windows-native-requirements-crosswalk) require a bounded, redacted crash-diagnostic boundary and a synthetic-secret crash-path test; [DD-22](../decisions/ADR-0017-DD-BATCH-CLOSURE.md) approves retention/export bounds but is not implemented here. This slice verifies only the **app-managed artifact surface after an abnormal exit**, on the current working-tree executable.
- **Procedure (bounded, reproducible):** `scripts/verify-mp-sec2-native.ps1` launches the current `cos-desktop.exe` twice in runtime mode with a **synthetic** observation token against a refused loopback endpoint (`http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>`), with `LOCALAPPDATA`/`TEMP`/`TMP` redirected to an isolated tree: one run is terminated abnormally (hard kill after the run has created its **own fresh** `desktop.instance`; the retained file is removed and its absence asserted before each launch) and one run must exit through a **delivered window close** (no fallback kill; `CloseMainWindow` failure invalidates the control), with exit code 0 and `preferences.json` written after that launch. The control runs **once** — there is no retry — and all three conditions (`close_requested`, exit 0, fresh `preferences.json`) must hold; the app's own shutdown notice is recorded as evidence but the file is the ground truth. Before any launch the script reads the credential store as **present / absent / unreadable**, aborts on present or unreadable, and never overwrites or deletes an entry it did not create; only entries observed as created by the run (or by the negative-test switch) are removed, and their absence is re-verified in the same three states. It then scans every app-managed file it can name — the isolated app-data tree (`desktop.instance`, the saved `preferences.json`), the isolated temp tree and both runs' stdout/stderr captures — for the token bytes with fixed limits (5,000 files, 4 MiB per file, depth 16). **PASS is strict:** all required roots and required artifacts must be present and fully scanned, with zero matches, zero unreadable/oversize/excluded entries and no walk cap; each per-area status (scan, control, abnormal run, credential) is derived from the same evidence as the overall verdict and exit code, an evidence-write failure forces FAIL, and any gap is HOLD. The synthetic credential must be observed after each launch and is deleted in an unconditional `finally` with its absence re-verified; a negative-test simulation records its write attempt before `cmdkey` runs, so an unreadable verification still removes that entry, and an entry that already existed is never touched. Any exception captured during the run forces FAIL, so no exception path can leave the verdict at PASS. Only child PIDs the script started are stopped (never a process by name); the work directory is GUID-unique and created exclusively; the negative-test switch is a closed enum whose resolved path is re-validated inside the work directory. It never uses a real credential, never touches the Runtime DB or the frozen fixtures, and never changes an OS setting.
- **Result (observed, 2026-11-01):** exe `35fdcd5b34d08c5d90242103a9285ffb4dd57fe889347a931d87d189c43f3bed` (34,954,752 bytes, `dev` HEAD `e522e5d`; Windows 11 Pro build 26300); 6 app-managed files scanned, 0 oversize, 0 unreadable, walk not capped, **0 token matches**; the abnormal run produced no stdout/stderr, and the normal control emitted only the static shutdown diagnostics (`observation shutdown confirmed`, `preferences save confirmed`). The synthetic credential entry the MP-SEC1 path stores by design under the synthetic origin was observed after each launch, removed in `finally`, and its absence re-verified. The hardened script PASSes on the recorded executable (exit 0), and its negative paths were exercised: removing a required artifact yields FAIL (exit 1), dropping the synthetic entry yields HOLD (exit 2), a wrong executable yields the precondition exit 3, a pre-existing credential aborts before launch (exit 3; with a real probe entry the stored secret was verified unchanged and the entry was left untouched), an out-of-tree negative-test path is rejected at parameter binding before any deletion, and a forced evidence-write failure or marker failure leaves no evidence file behind (FAIL, exit 1): both outputs are promoted only after every write succeeded and are sealed by a final completion marker that is itself written as `.complete.partial` and promoted by rename, and any rollback deletes the partials, the promoted files and the marker partial and re-verifies that they are gone (an artifact without a complete marker is never treated as official evidence).
- **Deliberately NOT covered (NOT_RUN/HOLD, never PASS):** WER user-mode dumps and the OS crash-report boundary (read-only check only: the machine `LocalDumps` key exists with no values configured, no per-user key, `WerSvc` stopped, and a hard kill does not invoke WER — no dump was induced or collected); crash dumps and any panic-path verification; other user profiles; process memory and pagefile; shell history; OS credential-store contents beyond existence/deletion (no plaintext read, no ACL claim); DD-22 retention/export and a bounded crash-report writer (not implemented in this slice). The support report is rendered in memory only, so there is no persisted report to scan.
- **Boundary:** this is a **limited native verification of app-managed artifacts after an abnormal exit**. It is not MP-SEC2 completion, not a crash/WER verification, and it does not claim that no secret can reach OS-managed crash surfaces. DD-22 open items are untouched.
- **Evidence:** a private evidence directory outside the repository; each run writes `mp-sec2-native-<utc>.json` and `.txt` with the exe SHA-256/size, OS/build, git HEAD, per-run command line and environment (the token replaced by its SHA-256), timings, stream hashes, the per-area status, scan roots/counts/matches/exclusions and the explicit NOT_RUN list. The token itself is never written to evidence.
- **Rust-side regression:** unchanged; the existing credential test already asserts that a rendered support report carries no token, and no second scan implementation is added to tests.

### 19.117 MP-AX1 AX04: High Contrast token selection and limited native verification (2026-11-01)

- **Scope:** [DC-MP-AX1](../architecture/DESKTOP_DESIGN_CONTRACTS.md#dc-mp-ax1) lists high contrast among the accessibility areas; the owner decision in §19.104 is that High Contrast is handled by **adding a high-contrast value set in the token layer** and switching when the OS setting is present, with the operator changing the OS setting manually. This slice implements that token-layer selection and a bounded native check; it does **not** complete MP-AX1.
- **Implementation (Desktop-local):** `crates/desktop-gpui/contrast.rs` owns two colour sets. `ContrastScheme::Normal` reuses the already-approved shell literals (root background `0x17191c`, text `0xe6e8eb`, focus `0xe6c278`, selection `0xaeccec`, border `0x626870`, muted `0x8b949e`); `ContrastScheme::HighContrast` maps **OS system colours** one role at a time (window, window text, highlight, highlight text, gray text, button face/button text) and invents nothing. Focus uses the system button-text colour so focus and selection stay distinct, and the token unit test pins focus ≠ selection ≠ disabled in both schemes. The Dock's focus ring and row colour now resolve through the scheme, as do the shell root background/text, the Dock group separator and formal-adoption label, and the Context Bar background (a fixed dark bar is unreadable under a dark OS text colour); a source-level test greps the delimited Dock region and the Context Bar for fixed palette literals. **Focus visibility is verified, not assumed:** the ring colour is chosen by WCAG contrast against the Dock surface — the focus role first, then the selection and text roles — so a near-identical focus colour falls back to a visible one; the focused Dock also draws the approved focus-outline width while the unfocused one uses a structural hairline. When every role collapses into the surface colour the token layer returns `FocusRing::Invisible` (the unit test classifies that case as invisible, never as visible-by-width); the shell still marks focus by width but claims no visible colour. The Dock container surface, the Dock rows, the Context Bar background and its state-axis text all resolve through the scheme; the Context Bar's state-axis labels are built by a separate `axis_cell` closure, whose muted label colour is now the scheme's disabled role (`0x8b949e` normally, the OS gray text under High Contrast) instead of a fixed literal. The Context Bar's stop/reconcile controls also resolve through the scheme (danger face/text/border, raised face, disabled face/text/border, muted text), with High Contrast mapping them to OS system colours only (highlight/highlight text/button text/gray text/window). **Their keyboard focus is never colour-only:** `shell_style::control_focus` reuses the Dock's visibility rule — focused draws the approved focus-outline width with a ring colour, unfocused the structural hairline — and the ring is chosen **against the button's actual background** (`danger_face`, `disabled_face`, `raised_face`), not the Dock surface, with `danger_text` added as an extra candidate on the danger face. A High Contrast palette that gives the focus colour and the resting border the same value still shows focus by border width (`a_same_colour_high_contrast_control_still_shows_focus_by_width`, including a white danger face where a white ring would vanish); the scale factor is validated before the focused/unfocused branch, so an unusable scale fails closed for focus as well; and `the_stop_controls_render_the_control_focus_result` pins that the render consumes the computed width/colour rather than a fixed border, counting the `control_focus` calls **only inside the delimited `stop-controls` region and requiring exactly two** (a global count would also match the test's own string; removing either call was verified to fail the test). The source-level guard now **sweeps five delimited regions** — Dock rows, the **whole Dock container** (any fixed colour, not just the old background value), the Context Bar block, the `axis_cell` closure and the `stop-controls` block — and any `rgb(0x` inside one of them fails the test; a full `grep` sweep of those regions reports **0 fixed colours**; the remaining 18 `rgb(0x` occurrences in `lib.rs` are **14 literals in render code outside the limited scope** (rail, inspector, palette, flow, compare hint) plus **4 matches inside the guard test's own strings** (the `!region.contains("rgb(0x")` assertions). `ContrastState::observe` rebuilds colours only and returns whether anything changed; the shell polls the registered probe every 2 s, runs the blocking OS query on the **background executor** (`background_executor().spawn`, never the UI thread) and repaints only on a colour change, so no restart is needed and a slow or failing query cannot stall drawing.
- **Probe (read-only):** `apps/desktop/src/contrast_probe.rs` reads `HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\HighContrast\Flags` (bit 0) and `HKCU\Control Panel\Colors` through the OS `reg query` — this crate forbids its own `unsafe`, so no Win32 signature is declared, and **no setting is changed**. The selection colours are stored under Windows' historical names **`Hilight` / `HilightText`**; the longer `Highlight`/`HighlightText` spellings are **implemented** as a legacy fallback (the canonical names win when both are present) and covered by a test. The first implementation looked for the long names only and therefore mis-reported "unavailable", which was a parser defect, not missing OS data. An incomplete or unreadable key still yields `None`, and the shell then keeps the normal palette rather than guessing.
- **Unit tests:** `contrast::tests::{the_normal_scheme_uses_the_approved_palette, the_high_contrast_scheme_uses_only_os_system_colors, focus_selection_and_disabled_are_distinct_in_both_schemes, a_switch_rebuilds_only_the_colour_state}` (the last covers the **colour state only** and claims no Shell view-state guarantee; that separation is structural — `Shell::observe_contrast` mutates its private colour field — and the native HC toggle is `NOT_RUN`), `contrast_probe::tests::{flags_bit_reads_the_scheme, the_system_colors_are_read_verbatim, the_legacy_selection_spellings_are_accepted, an_incomplete_colors_key_is_refused}` against a captured `reg query` output using the real `Hilight`/`HilightText` names, `lib.rs::contrast_scope_tests::the_limited_contrast_scope_contains_no_fixed_colour_literal` (Dock rows, Dock container, Context Bar), and the `shell_style` Dock tests (scheme-derived ring/row colours plus the `focus_ring` visibility and fallback assertions; a monochrome palette is classified `Invisible`, never claimed visible).
- **Measured natively (2026-11-01, corrected):** HC OFF — `HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\HighContrast\Flags` reads `REG_SZ 126` (bit 0 = 0) and the shell was captured in the normal palette (window 3456×1408, PNG + JSON record with exe SHA-256 `661b4069…`, graceful close, exit 0). With the corrected parser the runtime probe now reports **`contrast probe: Normal`** (traced); `HKCU\Control Panel\Colors` on this machine provides `Window 255 255 255`, `WindowText 0 0 0`, `Hilight 0 120 215`, `HilightText 255 255 255`, `GrayText 109 109 109`, `ButtonFace 240 240 240`, `ButtonText 0 0 0`. **High Contrast ON is `NOT_RUN`**: only the operator may change the OS setting, and no HC-on capture exists.
- **NOT MEASURED / NOT RUN (never PASS):** High Contrast ON (operator toggle required; not performed), HC-on focus/selection/disabled appearance and HC-on state preservation natively, DPI matrix, IME/TSF, screen-reader/AT acceptance, dialog focus restoration, reduced motion (NOT_APPLICABLE), and any claim that the whole shell (all surfaces) uses the scheme — this slice wires the root and Dock only. MP-AX1 remains incomplete and no product/UX acceptance follows.

### 19.118 MP-IMG2 Desktop: decode admission ceiling, worker ownership and unavailable classes (2026-11-01)

- **Scope:** the raster adapter in `crates/media/src/raster.rs` decodes the four admitted still containers (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) to RGBA8 under caller `DecodeLimits`. This slice states the decode bound accurately, bounds **concurrent** declared work with a process-wide reservation pool, and classifies unsupported input classes as typed `Unavailable`. No new format, GPU upload, WIC change, Runtime change or parallel framework is added, and MP-IMG2 is **not** declared complete; **no `BOUNDED_IMAGE_DECODE` completion is claimed**.
- **Admission ceiling, NOT a memory-peak proof:** `DECODER_BOOKKEEPING_BYTES` (1 MiB) is a **declared slack** with the same "assumed value" status as `DecodeBudget::ratified_default`, never a profiled figure. The admitted ceiling is `2 × (width × height × 4 B) + DECODER_BOOKKEEPING_BYTES` (decoded RGBA8 buffer + one same-size conversion buffer + declared slack), computed with checked arithmetic and checked **before the full-image decode and pixel-buffer allocation** (metadata parsing can allocate internally; that is outside this admission and not claimed to be covered): decoded ≤ `max_decoded_bytes`, declared scratch ≤ `max_scratch_bytes`, and the declared total ≤ their sum. This is an **admission decision over declared input geometry plus declared slack**; it does **not** prove the process's real memory peak, because decoder-internal allocations, the encoded input buffer, transport copies and other concurrent holders are outside the formula. **Real RSS/allocator peak per input class is `NOT_VERIFIED`** (never PASS); oversized or unmodelled classes remain `TooLarge`/`Unavailable` and are not admitted by inventing another constant.
- **Concurrent in-flight bound:** `admit_decode` is per-request, so a process-wide reservation counter (`AtomicU64`) now covers the declared ceilings of concurrent decodes. `decode_raster` reserves the admitted ceiling for the duration of the decode and releases it on drop; a request that would exceed the declared pool (`IN_FLIGHT_POOL_BYTES` = the declared decoded + scratch ceilings, 512 MiB, an assumed value) is refused **non-blocking** with the typed `MediaError::Busy` instead of waiting. The `MediaCache` payload budget is encoded-input accounting and remains separate. Tests: `decode::tests::in_flight_reservations_are_bounded_and_released` and `raster::tests::a_full_in_flight_pool_refuses_a_decode_without_blocking` (releases and succeeds after the holder drops). Because the pool is process-wide, **every** raster decode test takes the same `DECODE_TEST_LOCK` so a pool-filling test cannot race an ordinary decode under parallel `cargo test`; three consecutive workspace runs are reported in the review evidence.
- **Worker ownership, not a completion-time bound:** `decode_raster_joined` runs the decode on a `std::thread::scope` worker and **always joins** it, so a cancelled or failed decode cannot leave a decode thread behind. Cancellation is cooperative: it is observed only at the bounded checkpoints in `decode_raster` (before metadata, before the decoder call, after decode and after RGBA8 conversion); a cancellation arriving **inside** the decoder is observed at the next checkpoint, and `join` may wait for that decoder call to return. **Bounded cancellation / interruption of a running decoder is `NOT_VERIFIED` and held (HOLD)** — no completion-time guarantee is claimed, and this does not promote the initial profile. On `Cancelled` or any refusal no raster is returned, so no partial artifact can be published by this path. Tests: `a_cancelled_joined_decode_leaves_no_partial_raster`, `a_joined_decode_returns_a_complete_worker_result`, `a_cancel_at_the_pre_decode_checkpoint_publishes_no_raster` and `a_cancel_after_conversion_publishes_no_stale_raster` (synchronized test seam that cancels at a chosen checkpoint; no sleep).
- **Unavailable classes (typed, never silently rounded):** animated PNG (`acTL`), animated GIF (more than one image descriptor) and animated WebP (`ANIM`/`ANMF`) return `MediaError::Unavailable`; a source depth above 8 bits per channel or above the caller's `max_bit_depth` is `Unavailable`; an unadmitted container is `UnsupportedContainer`; oversized dimensions/bytes are `TooLarge`; corrupt or truncated payloads are `InvalidMetadata`. The still-image scan is bounded by the input length and stops at the first image data. Tests: `an_animated_png_is_unavailable`, `an_animated_gif_is_unavailable`, `an_animated_webp_is_unavailable_and_a_still_webp_is_not` (pure `ensure_still` scan over a minimal `ANIM` container; a still WebP is not misclassified), `a_sixteen_bit_png_is_unavailable_under_an_eight_bit_limit`, `refuses_a_corrupt_payload`, `refuses_an_unadmitted_container`, `refuses_dimensions_beyond_the_limits_before_decoding`.
- **NOT MEASURED / NOT VERIFIED (never PASS):** real process peak memory (RSS/allocator) and real decode latency/throughput per input class; decoder-internal peak allocations; bounded cancellation of a running decoder (HOLD); GPU upload, WIC behaviour, progressive JPEG and WebP animated features beyond the `ANIM`/`ANMF` marker; native/OS-level decoder measurement; any performance or memory SLO claim. MP-IMG2 as a whole remains incomplete and no `BOUNDED_IMAGE_DECODE` completion is claimed.
- **Boundaries:** the declared budgets and the in-flight pool remain owner-ratified assumed values; no Runtime, WIC, observation, transport or frozen-fixture contract is touched.

### 19.119 MP-IMG2 measured class: static 8-bit PNG (2026-11-01, Working Set route added)

- **Measured class:** static **8-bit RGB PNG, 2048 × 2048 px**, decoded to RGBA8 under the ratified declared budget (`DecodeBudget::ratified_default`). Declared admission ceiling `2 × (2048 × 2048 × 4 B) + 1,048,576 B = **34,603,008 B**`. The 64 × 64 case remains a functional case in the same test binary, not the measurement target.
- **Safe measurement route (no `unsafe`):** `crates/media/examples/peak_probe.rs` generates the class fixture in-process, signals `fixture-ready`, waits for a go file, then decodes once. `scripts/measure-decode-peak.ps1` starts that process, samples `WorkingSet64` every 10 ms, records a pre-decode baseline, the peak and the end value, and writes JSON/TXT evidence outside the repository. No OS setting and no credential is touched.
- **Measured (5 runs, 2026-11-01, hardened judge + decode-phase sample counting):** each run is only counted when the probe **exited 0**, reported the **complete RGBA8 output (16,777,216 B)**, and had **at least `MinDecodeSamples` (3) samples whose decode-start marker existed and decode-done marker did not, checked both immediately before and immediately after the sample** (the parameter is validated: a value below 3 is refused with a non-zero exit, so the condition cannot be disabled by an argument) (markers bracket the decode call; boundary granularity is one 10 ms sampling interval). A run failing any condition makes the verdict **FAIL**, never PASS. Result: 5/5 valid runs, baseline 5,283,840–5,357,568 B, peak 35,061,760–35,131,392 B, **increment median 29,777,920 B / max 29,782,016 B**, decode-phase samples 16–17 per run; ceiling 34,603,008 B → **Working Set condition PASS** (max is 4,820,992 B = 4.60 MiB below the ceiling). Negative controls: (1) an over-limit 20,000 px class produced a small increment but was **FAIL** (exit 1, no complete output); (2) a run with **correct output length and exit 0 but too few decode-phase samples** (`-MinDecodeSamples 100`) was also **FAIL** (exit 1), so the sample-count gate is discriminating on its own.
- **Measurement limit (recorded, not hidden):** Working Set is **process-wide** and includes the in-process generated fixture, runtime and mapping pages; it is **not an allocation peak**. Sampling is 10 ms, so a shorter-lived peak can be missed, and `Get-Process` overhead bounds the sampling rate. This row must not be read as an allocator measurement.
- **Allocator row stays HOLD:** the instructed counting global allocator still needs `unsafe impl GlobalAlloc`, and the workspace forbids own-code `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`, not relaxable by `allow`); no existing seam or approved test dependency exists. Unblock options remain (a) a narrow documented exception for a test-only allocator, (b) an approved test-support workspace member, (c) an approved dev-dependency providing a counting allocator (allowlist and checker updated together). The Working Set row is **separate** and is not substituted for it.
- **Judgment table:**

| Condition | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Class definition (static 8-bit RGB PNG 2048×2048) | **PASS** | `crates/media/tests/measured_png_class.rs`, `examples/peak_probe.rs` |
| Declared admission ceiling (34,603,008 B) | **PASS** | formula pinned in the test/plan |
| **Real memory: Working Set peak increment ≤ ceiling** | **PASS** | 5-run harness: max 29,782,016 B ≤ 34,603,008 B (decode-phase samples 16–17/run) |
| Real internal peak (allocator measurement) | **CLOSED** | `peak_alloc` as an approved dev-only dependency (§19.233); 2048×2048 PNG increment **17,198,408 B** ≤ 34,603,008 B (§19.251) |
| Worker lifetime: joined before return | **PASS** | `std::thread::scope` + `join()` in `decode_raster_joined`, plus the complete-raster assertion; no product-side counter exists |
| Cancellation is typed and publishes nothing | **PASS** | pre-cancelled call asserts exactly `Err(MediaError::Cancelled)` and no raster |
| Rejection typed and no output published | **PASS** | 20,000 px input → `TooLarge`; slot empty |
| Rejection allocation flatness | **CLOSED** | PNG refusals 80,800 / 151,712 / 151,712 B over a 16× area span (§19.233); the absolute bound alone was insufficient, so a relative growth bound is asserted too |
| Bounded cancellation of a running decoder | **PASS for non-interlaced PNG; HOLD for every other class** | the product path runs the row decoder for non-interlaced PNG (§19.240): external cancel mid-decode stopped after row 9 of 3000 and returned 253–564 µs later (§19.241); interlaced PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF remain uninterruptible |
| **JPEG class peak** | **PASS** | 2048×2048 increment **29,360,328 B** ≤ 34,603,008 B (§19.251) |
| **JPEG refusal shape** | **PASS** | 12,950 / 13,865 / 31,021 B over a 16× area span; absolute and relative bounds asserted (§19.251) |
| **WebP class peak** | **PASS** | 1024×1024 increment **7,342,044 B** ≤ 9,437,184 B (§19.252) |
| **WebP refusal shape** | **PASS (byte-ceiling kind)** | **516 B at all three areas** under a 64,000 B byte ceiling, i.e. flat (§19.254). A *dimension* refusal remains unbuildable; an earlier note calling the refusal generally unconstructible was too strong |
| **GIF class peak** | **PASS** | 1024×1024 increment **5,281,574 B** ≤ 9,437,184 B (§19.252) |
| **GIF refusal shape** | **PASS** | **9,142 B** at all three areas, i.e. flat (§19.252) |
| **16-bit PNG** | **REFUSED as `Unavailable`** | a 512×512 16-bit PNG is not decoded; the refusal allocates **151,712 B** against the **1,048,576 B** a decode would need (§19.255) |
| **Other sizes** | **PASS (512×512 measured)** | ceiling scales with area: **1,463,624 B** ≤ **3,145,728 B** at 512×512 (§19.255) |
| Other depths and sizes beyond these | **NOT_VERIFIED** | out of this slice |
| MP-IMG2 overall completion | **NOT CLAIMED** | — |

- **Worker-lifetime evidence:** there is no product-side worker counter (a caller-side increment would measure joined-call concurrency, not live workers, and the scope join already guarantees collection). The evidence is the language-level `std::thread::scope` + `join()` in `decode_raster_joined`, the complete-raster check, and the typed-`Cancelled`/no-publication test.
- **MP-IMG3 start decision:** the Working Set condition is now proven **at process scope**, but the internal allocator peak and running-decoder cancellation remain unproven. Under the reviewer's literal rule ("実メモリ・worker 寿命・拒否・出力公開の全条件"), the class is still **HOLD**; a **limited start** is defensible only if the reviewer explicitly accepts the Working Set measurement as the real-memory evidence for this class. This slice does not declare MP-IMG2 complete and does not start MP-IMG3 on its own authority.

### 19.120 MP-R0B idle baseline: disconnected variant, five reproducible runs (2026-11-01)

- **Scope and authority:** bounded R0B idle-baseline measurement using the existing launch pattern (`cos-desktop.exe` in runtime mode against an unreachable loopback endpoint), per the §19.106 authorization for a fresh idle baseline. No new dependency or framework; no OS setting, Runtime DB or fixture change.
- **Harness:** `scripts/measure-r0b-idle.ps1` (PowerShell only). The approved conditions are **mandatory parameters**: exactly **5 runs**, **30 s settle**, **60 s observation**, **500 ms sampling**; any other value is refused with exit 2 instead of producing a weaker PASS. Each run is a fresh process with `COS_DESKTOP_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9`, and validity additionally requires **≥ 115 samples**, an **observed first-to-last sample span ≥ 59 s**, `window_completed`, exit code 0 and the `Runtime observation unavailable` line. Run directories are created **exclusively with a GUID** and only that directory is deleted; the child process is reaped in `finally`.
- **Identity binding (before launch):** the harness pins the executable SHA-256 (`2357f0418cee8c49802bfdd5b77452fed5d1e63a18b824e9c6fa5b4a6222beb9`) **before the first launch**, re-hashes it immediately before each run and after each run, and records source identity: HEAD `d6b433b8b3ed3f8ced432d4a213ccbb927118655`, dirty=true (1 uncommitted entry), build kind `debug (cargo build --locked)`. Any mismatch is **HOLD** (exit 3), never a late-derived identifier.
- **Endpoint availability (recorded):** `http://127.0.0.1:9` is **unavailable (connection refused)**. Every figure below is therefore a **disconnected baseline**; it is not a connected-endpoint baseline and must not be read as one.
- **Measured (5 valid runs; CPU = fraction of one core, WS = mean working set):** CPU 0.009104 / WS 70,905,044 B; 0.029160 / 70,893,180 B; 0.017303 / 70,976,013 B; 0.004942 / 70,715,674 B; 0.033333 / 70,834,684 B. Observed spans 59.494–59.995 s, samples 116–117 per run.
- **Aggregates:** CPU — **median 0.017303, mean 0.018768, stddev 0.012317, noise (CV) 65.6 %** (the spread is reported as measured, not smoothed). Working set — **median 70,893,180 B (≈ 67.6 MiB), mean 70,864,919 B, stddev 97,389 B, noise 0.137 %**.

| Metric | Result | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| CPU idle baseline, disconnected endpoint | **PASS_LIMITED** | 5 valid runs, CV 65.6 % reported as measured |
| Working-set idle baseline, disconnected endpoint | **PASS_LIMITED** | 5 valid runs, sampling noise 0.137 % |

- **Evidence completeness:** the record stores **every sample series** (582 rows: `at_s`, `cpu_s`, `cpu_delta_s`, `working_set_bytes` per sample) so each run's mean/stddev can be recomputed independently.
- **Negative paths (measured):** `-Runs 0` / `-SettleSeconds 1` / `-WindowSeconds 30` are **refused with exit 2**; a short observation (`-SimulateEarlyExitSeconds 5`, 11 samples, span ≈ 5.2 s) is **invalid with exit 1**; a run whose executable hash does not match the pinned identity (`-SimulateExeMismatch`) is **HOLD with exit 3**.
- **Unresolved R0A/R0B conditions (not hidden):** §19.91's earlier idle attempt remains `HOLD_APPROVED_ARTIFACTS_AND_CAPTURE_CONDITIONS_UNAVAILABLE` (approved instrumented executable/helper/source admission missing; the complete R0 suite ran 352 cases and exited 1 with **1 failure / 11 errors / 12 skipped**, including the live-metadata observer-digest mismatch and eleven R0C `SOURCE_IDENTITY` cases). MP-R0A overall is `IN_PROGRESS`: S2B full-source replay is pending and S3-N1 stays a limited source/retained-journal/evidence completion that does not close DC-MP-R0A (full source-bound replay, independent binary/source verification, Present/displayed/scanout/GPU/input-to-photon, visible-stall attribution, queue/cancellation/restoration and performance distributions outstanding). This slice does not restore those conditions and does not repeat the failed R0 suite.
