### 19.121 MP-FLOW2 10,000-node bottleneck and minimal Stage (2026-11-01, product-path corrected)

- **Scope and method:** one deterministic synthetic graph of **10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges** (100 layers × 100 nodes, two edges per node into the next layer) measured with the **existing** `flow.rs` phases in an explicit `#[ignore]` test. The measurement now mirrors the **product render path**: `flow_diagram_region` rebuilds both match sets from the admitted rows on every render, so the frame measurement builds the populated `BTreeSet<(GraphRef, NodeId)>` (10,000 entries) and `BTreeSet<(GraphRef, EdgeId)>` (19,800 entries) and passes them into `diagram()`. No product-code change, no new dependency, no `unsafe`, no custom renderer. Iterations **20 measured + 3 warm-up**; medians and p95 are computed **from the measured per-iteration totals**, not by adding phase medians.
- **Equivalence (no behaviour change):** the construction reference, an **independent Kahn longest-path** and the implementation's `layers()` produce the same depth vector; `cyclic == false`; `rows_cancellable()` admits every node/edge in authoritative order; `diagram()` draws the first **120** nodes in authoritative order, every drawn depth equals the reference, and `drawn edges + skipped edges == 19,800`. Deterministic FNV checksum **`0x1cfce993dc07a7c8`** in both debug and release.
- **Measured, release profile (phase references, 20 iterations, even-count median = mean of the two middle values):** rows 603 µs / p95 820 µs; `layers` 5,044 / 5,751 µs; **match-set build 10,698 / 11,490 µs**; `diagram` 3,059 / 3,475 µs; connector geometry 19 / 21 µs.
- **Measured per-render totals (decision series):** **frame path (match sets + `diagram`) 13,849 µs median / 14,579 µs p95** (max 14,797 µs); **full recompute baseline (rows + layers + match sets + diagram + geometry) 19,228 µs median / 21,053 µs p95** (max 21,450 µs). Run-to-run spread is reported as measured (an earlier run of the same code measured 12,888 / 13,282 µs); the conclusion does not depend on the spread.
- **Debug profile (limits the claim):** rows 1,913 µs, layers 20,303 µs, diagram 10,025 µs, geometry 61 µs, total 32,302 µs (earlier run; the release profile is the evidence basis).
- **Bottleneck ranking (release, frame path):** **match-set construction 10.70 ms (77.2 %)** ≫ `diagram` 3.06 ms (22.1 %) ≫ rows/geometry (revision/negligible). The earlier "4.91 ms steady state" did not represent the product path because it omitted the populated match sets; with them, the per-frame CPU path is **13.85 ms median / 14.58 ms p95**.
- **Minimal Stage decision: Stage C is required (not implemented in this slice).** Culling (Stage B) cannot address this ranking — the drawn geometry is 19 µs and the cost is rebuilding the revision-wide match sets and drawing. The **initial Stage C scope is the cached match-set build only** (the 10.7 ms dominant term), invalidated by the **existing complete admission identity `flow::AdmissionKey`** — session generation, publication version, epoch, revision and query — not by revision/query alone, so an authorization or session change can never reuse a stale set. **Diagram caching is not part of the initial scope**: it is added only if a follow-up measurement shows it is still necessary after the match-set cache (nothing is implemented here). `layers` is already revision-cached. The measured current path exceeds the **8.33 ms UI p95** target, so "current implementation maintained" is **not** justified by the corrected numbers. Stage D–F remain unimplemented (no LOD, batching or custom renderer).
- **Judgment:**

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| CPU layout phases at 10,000 nodes (release) | **PASS_LIMITED** (one machine, synthetic graph; medians/p95 from totals) |
| Graph equivalence / determinism | **PASS_LIMITED** (Kahn reference, depth vector, rows order, diagram cap, checksum) |
| Per-frame CPU path ≤ 8.33 ms UI p95 | **HOLD** (14,579 µs p95) |
| Per-frame CPU path ≤ 60 Hz 16.67 ms | **PASS_LIMITED** (median 13,849 µs; leaves ≈ 2.8 ms for paint/GPU) |
| Full recompute baseline ≤ 60 Hz | **HOLD** (19,228 µs median) |
| Paint / submit / GPU / Present / input-to-photon | **NOT_MEASURED** |
| Real hardware matrix, 120 Hz target | **HOLD** (single machine, no GPU) |
| Runtime-bound graph | **NOT_MEASURED** (synthetic graph only) |
| MP-FLOW2 overall / Stage D–F | **not claimed / not implemented** |

- **Measurement limits:** release vs debug differ (~3×, reported); single machine; synthetic topology; timer excludes GPUI paint/layout, GPU and Present; trace-instrumented frame times on target hardware remain the missing endpoint. The judgment is an inherited CPU observation, not an SLO attainment.
- **No product change:** only the ignored measurement test was edited; the render path, contracts and budgets are unchanged.

### 19.122 MP-FLOW2 Stage C: bounded match-set cache (2026-11-01)

- **Scope (limited):** only the **revision-wide match sets** (`Matched.nodes` / `Matched.edges`) that `flow_diagram_region` rebuilt on every render are cached. The **diagram is not cached** (added only if a follow-up measurement shows it is still needed after this slice). No Stage D–F, no new dependency, no `unsafe`, no custom renderer, no GPUI pin change.
- **Structure and ownership:** `flow::Matched` + `flow::MatchCache` in `crates/desktop-gpui/src/flow.rs`; the cache is a **single-entry** `Option<(AdmissionKey, Arc<Matched>)>` owned by the existing `Shell` (`flow_match_cache`), never a global. `get_or_build` returns `(Arc<Matched>, hit)`; a miss replaces the one entry, so the cache is bounded by construction. When the admission key is absent (non-current revision) the region builds transiently and never touches the cache, so existing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Invalidation:** the **complete `flow::AdmissionKey`** — `session_generation`, `publication_version`, `epoch`, `revision`, `query` — is the key. Unit tests prove each component invalidates: `the_match_cache_invalidates_on_every_admission_key_component` (five variants, one per component, each a miss with one entry retained), plus `the_match_cache_stays_bounded_under_many_keys` (16 keys, `len() == 1`) and `a_cached_match_set_draws_the_same_diagram_as_an_uncached_build` (identical `Diagram`).
- **Equivalence:** the cached diagram is **`==`** to the uncached build (same nodes, depths, lanes, edges, cap and counts; `Diagram` derives `PartialEq`), and the 10,000-node checksum stays **`0x1cfce993dc07a7c8`**. The measurement also asserts the miss diagram equals the pre-cache diagram and every hit draws the identical diagram.
- **Measured before/after (release, 10,000 nodes, 20 iterations; even-count medians = mean of the two middle values, p95 nearest-rank):**

| Path | median | p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| before (uncached frame path: match sets + diagram) | 12,761 µs | 15,125 µs |
| after (cached steady frame: cache hit + diagram) | **2,586 µs** | **2,975 µs** |
| first frame after (cache miss: build sets + diagram, single sample) | **13,000 µs** | — |
| saved per steady frame (median, same run: 12,761 − 2,586) | **10,175 µs** | — |

- **Budget:** the cached steady frame is **2,975 µs p95 ≤ 8,330 µs** (same-run headroom 5,355 µs; earlier runs measured 3.0–3.3 ms p95, reported as measured spread) — the 8.33 ms UI p95 CPU target is met for this path. A cache **miss occurs on every `AdmissionKey` change** — revision, publication_version, query, epoch or session generation — not only on a graph revision; the first frame after a miss measured 13.0 ms in this run (13.7–17.6 ms in earlier runs) and how often such a change happens in operation is **NOT_MEASURED**. The full recompute baseline (rows+layers+match sets+diagram) measured **18,348 µs median / 22,073 µs p95 in the same run, above the 16.67 ms 60 Hz frame** → **HOLD** (no "inside 60 Hz" claim).
- **Judgment:**

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Match-set cache: hit/miss, per-component invalidation, boundedness | **PASS_LIMITED** (unit tests; single machine) |
| Diagram equivalence (cached == uncached, checksum) | **PASS_LIMITED** |
| Steady frame CPU path ≤ 8.33 ms UI p95 | **PASS_LIMITED** (2,975 µs p95) |
| Cold first frame / full recompute after a miss | **HOLD** (13.0 ms first frame / 18.35 ms full recompute median; misses follow every AdmissionKey change, frequency NOT_MEASURED) |
| Paint / submit / GPU / Present / input-to-photon | **NOT_MEASURED** |
| Real hardware matrix, 120 Hz | **HOLD** |
| Runtime-bound graph | **NOT_MEASURED** |
| MP-FLOW2 overall / Stage D–F | **not claimed / not implemented** |

- **Limits:** release profile, single machine, synthetic 100×100 topology, `Instant` phase attribution excludes GPUI paint/layout, GPU and Present; the cached values are a bounded local observation, not an SLO attainment. The cache is per shell and per revision; it does not change graph identity, topology, admission or cancellation behaviour.

### 19.123 MP-IMG2 one-class proof: Job Object hard cap and measured cancellation (2026-11-01, joined path)

- **Class:** static **8-bit RGB PNG 2048×2048**, decoded to RGBA8 with the expected complete output **16,777,216 B**, probe `crates/media/examples/peak_probe.rs`, harness `scripts/measure-img2-job.ps1`. No new dependency, no `unsafe`, no GPU upload, no product-code change.
- **Memory bound by hard constraint (no allocator instrumentation):** the harness creates a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_MEMORY | JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, starts the probe **suspended**, assigns it to the job and only then resumes it (the cap applies from the first instruction). A 4 MiB binary search finds: **32 MiB (33,554,432 B) — normal completion with the complete 16,777,216 B output (confirmed twice)**; **28 MiB (29,360,128 B) — no normal completion (confirmed)**. **The unrestricted real peak is NOT_MEASURED**, and no interval for the actual peak is claimed: the 28 MiB failure was not attributed to a memory-limit violation specifically, so only the two bounded statements above stand. A 1 MiB search was attempted first and was not stable at the boundary (29 MiB succeeded on a re-run after failing during the search), so the reported points use the stable 4 MiB step.
- **Measurement limit:** the Job cap limits **whole-process commit** (in-process generated fixture, Rust runtime, decoder working set); it is not a decoder-only allocation figure and not an allocator-profile peak.
- **Cancellation (product joined path):** the probe now calls **`decode_raster_joined()`**, which owns the scoped worker and joins it before returning; cancellation is requested via a file while the decode is running. The probe records `decode-start-at-ms`, `cancel-at-ms` and `decode-returned-at-ms` and reports `cancel-within-decode`; the harness **rejects a run unless the cancel instant lies between the start and return markers**, the result is typed `Cancelled`, the exit code is 0 and no residual probe process exists. **5/5 runs** satisfied all of that. Observed parent-side latency: 335, 345, 348, 348, 353 ms (**median 348 ms, max 353 ms**); probe-internal delay 320–335 ms; total decode 387–388 ms.
- **Honest bound:** the observed latency is **not a worst-case stop guarantee**. The image decoder is not interruptible during the call, so the delay is bounded by the remaining decode time (cancel at 50 ms of a ≈ 390 ms debug decode). **Interruptible/preemptible running-decoder cancellation remains `NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD`.**
- **Failure-path cleanup (measured negatives):** the job is created with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. The launch helper keeps the process/thread handles in **one `finally`** and hands the process handle off only on success, so a real API failure cannot double-release. Termination is a separate step: `TerminateProcess` return is checked, then `WaitForSingleObject` confirms the exit; a failure of either surfaces **`recovery-unverified:<detail>`**, which the harness reports as **HOLD (exit 3)**, never PASS. `AssignProcessToJobObject`, `ResumeThread` and `TerminateProcess` declare `SetLastError = true` and record their Win32 error numbers in `assign-failed:<err>` / `resume-failed:<err>` / `recovery-unverified:terminate-failed:<err>`. Measured negatives: `-SimulateAssignFailure` and `-SimulateResumeFailure` → `reached_route=True`, residual 0, **PASS (exit 0)**; `-SimulateRecoveryUnverified` → **HOLD (exit 3)**; a deliberately unplanned failure → `reached_route=False`, **FAIL (exit 1)**. The negative record stores `expected_route`, `reached_route`, `captured_error`, `verdict` and `residual_after` (no stale `failed_as_expected` field). A cap run with a **WorkRoot containing spaces** also passed (all CreateProcess arguments are quoted).
- **Judgment:**

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Normal completion under a 32 MiB whole-process Job cap | **PASS_LIMITED** (confirmed twice) |
| No normal completion under a 28 MiB whole-process Job cap | **PASS_LIMITED** (confirmed) |
| Unrestricted real peak / allocator-level peak | **NOT_MEASURED** (not claimed; `unsafe_code = "forbid"` for the allocator) |
| Output completeness 16,777,216 B | **PASS_LIMITED** |
| Joined worker: typed `Cancelled`, cancel inside the decode interval, no residual process | **PASS_LIMITED** (5/5) |
| Observed cancellation latency (median 348 / max 353 ms) | **PASS_LIMITED** (observed, not a worst-case bound) |
| Interruptible (preemptible) cancellation / bounded worst-case stop | **NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD** |
| Rejection typed / no partial publication | **PASS** (previous slice) |
| Other classes, paint/GPU/real hardware/120 Hz | **NOT_MEASURED / HOLD** |
| MP-IMG2 overall, R4 overall | **not claimed** |

- **MP-IMG3 decision:** a **limited start** is defensible only if the reviewer accepts the **32 MiB whole-process cap completion** as the memory evidence for this class and the **observed remaining-decode-time latency** as the cancellation bound; on the literal "internal memory or running-cancel ceiling proven" rule the class remains **HOLD**. This slice does not start MP-IMG3 on its own authority.

### 19.124 MP-SEC2 4096 ring, sequence/gap, support report and redaction limits (2026-11-02)

- **Authority:** ADR-0017 DD-22 already ratifies an in-memory ring of **4,096 records**; the older DC-MP-PUB1 bound (1,024) and the code constant were stale. The design-order change is included here: `DESKTOP_DESIGN_CONTRACTS.md` now states **4,096** in both normative clauses, and `crates/app-core/src/diagnostics.rs` fixes `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS = 4096`.
- **A. Retention proven:** `the_ring_retains_exactly_the_declared_cap_and_evicts_the_oldest` (5,000 appends: retained exactly 4,096, oldest = 905, latest = 5,000, one gap 1–904, strictly increasing sequences) and `retention_never_exceeds_the_cap_at_any_append` (every append up to 8,192 checked). The observation-level test now overflows with `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS + 100` events and asserts 4,096 retained, gap `start+1..start+100`, and per-event sequences from `start+101`.
- **B. Sequence and gap:** monotone non-reusing sequence (existing exhaustion test), `a_continuous_stream_never_reports_a_gap` (updates the cursor every event across 8,192 appends), `normal_eviction_does_not_fake_a_gap_for_a_current_cursor` (eviction alone is not loss; only a cursor that fell behind gets the exact prefix), and `a_real_discontinuity_is_reported_once_as_one_interval` (one interval 101–500, not one per lost event; advancing the cursor past it reports nothing).
- **C. Support report consistency (ring scope, option (a)):** `DiagnosticBatch` now carries ring-wide statistics — `retained_events`, `oldest_retained_sequence` and `retained_counts` (`DiagnosticCounts` moved to `diagnostics` and re-exported) — maintained **incrementally by the ring** on append/eviction, so a report never mixes ring-wide and cursor-window numbers. `DiagnosticsSummary::from_batch` restates them instead of recomputing from `batch.events`; `event_gap_lost` states the numeric lost count. The mixed-case test `the_report_restates_the_ring_retention_not_the_cursor_window` uses a self-consistent fixture (contiguous ring 906..=5001 = 4,096 events, window 5000–5001) and asserts all three rendered lines: `Retained events: 4096`, `Oldest retained: 906` (never the window's 5000) and `Event counts: activity 4095, connection 0, error 0, resync 1` (never the window's 1/0/0/1); it also asserts the invariant `latest − oldest + 1 == retained` and that the category sum equals the retained count.
- **D. Redaction and output bounds:** numeric assertions on `Limits: events 4096, line 512 bytes, report 12288 bytes, 24 lines`; every rendered line ≤ 512 bytes and the report ≤ 12,288 bytes; a boundary line of repeated multi-byte characters is truncated on a UTF-8 boundary and stays valid. The synthetic-credential/private-path test remains green. **Defect found and fixed:** the limits and event-count lines used ` / ` separators, which the path redactor classified as private paths and mangled into `[private-path]`; separators are now commas, and the exact limits line is asserted.
- **E. Gates:** fmt, metadata, dependency checker + self-test, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --locked --workspace` = **699 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored** (36 binaries), build OK.
- **F. Not implemented (recorded, not claimed):** crash-report retention (DD-22's three 5 MiB crash reports), the Windows Error Reporting boundary, and persistence of diagnostics across process restart. The ring is in-memory only. DD-22 export/destination/consent details remain open.
- **Judgment:** retention/sequence/gap/report/redaction/limits for the in-process ring are **PASS_LIMITED** (bounded local observation); crash reports, WER and persistence are **NOT_IMPLEMENTED / HOLD**. **MP-SEC2 overall is not claimed complete**, and no R4/Runtime/UX approval follows.
- **Next recommended:** a separate MP-SEC2 slice for the crash-report ring (3 × 5 MiB, redacted) and the WER boundary decision, then an independent SEC2 review.

### 19.125 MP-SEC2 bounded crash-report storage (2026-11-02)

- **Scope:** safe explicit save / generation management / restart read-back for crash reports, per ADR-0017 DD-22. Automatic crash capture and WER control are **not** part of this slice.
- **A. Storage boundary (implemented):** `app-core::crash_report` derives the only location from the existing application data path — `preferences::default_path().parent()?.join("crash-reports")` — and exposes `open_default()` for that derivation plus `open_at()` for tests. There is no caller-supplied production path and no fallback location. The root is checked with `symlink_metadata` before and after creation and on every `list`/`read`: a file, symlink, junction or any other reparse point (`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`) is refused as `NotADirectory`, so writes and eviction can never be redirected outside the dedicated directory (verified by a junction/symlink negative that leaves the target empty).
- **B. Capacity and retention (implemented):** `MAX_CRASH_REPORTS = 3`, `MAX_CRASH_REPORT_BYTES = 5_242_880`. A fourth save deletes **only the oldest managed regular file** before writing; startup (`open_*`, `prune`) trims managed reports beyond three and removes a managed report larger than the ceiling. A candidate larger than the ceiling is refused **before** staging. The managed name is fixed at ten digits (`MAX_REPORT_ID = 9_999_999_999`); when the next sequence would exceed it, `save` fails with `IdExhausted` **before any eviction or write**. **This guarantee is limited to the ID-ceiling refusal**: it does not cover failures after a write is attempted. On the normal rotation path the oldest retained report is deleted before `commit()`, so a later write/sync/rename failure leaves the new report unpublished **and the evicted report is not restored** — an accepted trade-off of the evict-before-write design, tracked separately from the ID-ceiling fix. Managed name shape is exactly `report-<10 ASCII digits>.txt`; unknown files, malformed names, directories and symlinks are never read, listed, evicted or replaced.
- **C. Secrecy (implemented):** the report input is closed — desktop version string, closed `CrashCategory`, and the ring's safe diagnostic summary — with **no free-text field**, so a panic payload or remote text has no storage path. Every line is rendered with `redact_diagnostic_text_within(…, 512)`; a line that changes on a second redaction pass, or a version containing control characters, is refused as `UnsafeContent` **without writing**. Synthetic credential/signed-locator/private-path input is redacted and asserted absent from the stored file.
- **D. Write integrity (implemented):** the body is bounded, written to `.staged-<pid>-<nanos>-<seq>.tmp` **inside the dedicated directory** with `create_new`, `write_all`, `sync_all`, then renamed to the final managed name; only a staging file **this call created** is cleaned up: `create_new` collisions leave the existing file untouched, and every failure after creation (write, sync, rename) removes it. A cleanup failure surfaces as `StagingCleanup` instead of being ignored, and `list`/`read` never treat a staging file as a report. `prune()` re-checks the root first, so a store directory replaced by a link/junction after creation is refused before any managed report is deleted. A negative test makes the finalize rename fail (a directory at the final name) and asserts zero `.staged-*` residue and that the blocking directory is untouched. Startup inspection touches only managed regular files.
- **E. Tests (18 new):** unit (11) — root derivation; exact 5 MiB commit accepted and one byte over refused pre-write; control-character input refused as `UnsafeContent` with nothing listed; startup prune keeps only the newest three managed reports; a pure `is_link_or_reparse(attributes, is_symlink)` predicate is tested on ordinary, reparse-point, symlink and combined attribute words without creating a link; a linked/junction root is refused with an empty target, and if the environment cannot create a link the test **fails** (a skipped check is not evidence); a failed finalize leaves no staging file; the sequence stops at the ten-digit name limit (`IdExhausted`, one file); `prune()` refuses a store directory replaced by a link/junction and the target-side report survives; three retained reports at the ID ceiling survive an **ID-refused** save completely; a staging-name collision preserves the pre-existing file. Integration (7) — 1–3 saves and reload in order; fourth save evicts only the oldest managed report; synthetic secrets absent from the stored bytes; no staging residue after success and a file-as-directory is refused; a new store instance reloads reports (restart); a **ten-digit** managed-looking directory and a link survive rotation and pruning; declared bounds equal the ratified values.
- **F. Gates:** fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --locked --workspace`, build, dependency checker (see the task report for counts).
- **G. Judgment:** explicit save, rotation, redaction and restart read-back are **PASS_LIMITED** (bounded local observation; the API is exercised by tests, not yet wired to an automatic crash handler). **HOLD / NOT_RUN:** automatic on-crash report generation, WER dump/OS-managed-area secrecy, 4,096-event ring persistence across restart, report export/consent UI, and **MP-SEC2 overall**.

### 19.126 MP-SEC2 Windows WER boundary: native evidence (2026-11-02)

- **A. Environment pinned (read-only):** HEAD `32cac6295de896e9c400d3d97c1e74d73af7aab6` with 1 dirty entry (this script/plan); `target/debug/cos-desktop.exe` SHA-256 `2e53072f08f227937bbed0c956b704f9b548980b705afff5b198a083859b8a5a`, 35,048,448 B; **Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x64**, PowerShell 7.6.9. The existing `scripts/verify-mp-sec2-native.ps1` was extended; no new verification framework was added.
- **B. WER configuration read (three states, nothing changed):** `disabled_state = enabled` (`Disabled` value not set; **WerSvc Running**); **machine `LocalDumps` key present with no value names** (no DumpFolder/DumpType/DumpCount); **user `LocalDumps` absent**; exe-specific `LocalDumps\cos-desktop.exe` and `LocalDumps\powershell.exe` **absent** in both hives. No registry write, no WER setting change.
- **C. Controlled abnormal exit:** one **disposable `powershell.exe` child** executed `[Environment]::FailFast(...)` with a synthetic token; **exit code −2,146,232,797 (0x80131623)**, duration 7,000 ms, real unhandled exception. The **production Desktop process was never crashed** (`intentionally_production_desktop = false`); the conclusion is not a Desktop-specific crash verification.
- **D. Artifact and boundary:** one artifact appeared in the **OS-managed area**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\powershell.exe.<pid>.dmp`, size **27,312,167 B**, owner `DIO\diobrando`, extension `.dmp`. A **bounded** scan (first + last **1,048,576 B**; 2,097,152 B total) found **0** synthetic-token matches. Raw artifact bytes were never copied into evidence. The Desktop-managed `crash-reports` directory was **empty before and after** (unchanged), so the app-managed area and the OS-managed CrashDumps area are recorded as distinct boundaries.
- **B-01 (fixed):** the WER status now propagates: `HOLD` → overall **HOLD (exit 2)**; `NOT_RUN` (skipped child) → **PASS_LIMITED (exit 0)** with `checks.wer_verified = false` and `wer_boundary = NOT_RUN`, so the limited overall success is never reported as WER-verified. Measured: normal `PASS_LIMITED/0` (`wer_verified=true`), `-SkipWerChildCrash` `PASS_LIMITED/0` (`wer_verified=false`), `-SimulateWerHold` `HOLD/2`.
- **B-02 (fixed):** artifacts are correlated with the crashed child — the name must start with `powershell.exe.<child pid>.`; unrelated new files are recorded separately and never count as evidence; `real_unhandled_exception` is true only when the exit code equals the FailFast code **−2,146,232,797**. Measured: `correlated=1, unrelated=0, failfast_match=True` for pid 8216; the simulated-hold run has a real dump (27,449,960 B) yet `correlated=0` and correctly stays HOLD.
- **B-03 (fixed):** the bounded scan searches **UTF-8 and UTF-16LE**; an always-on self-test scans a synthetic UTF-16LE token (`matches_utf16le=1`) and `-SimulateUtf16Miss` forces FAIL (exit 1). `-WerScanBytes 0` is refused with exit 2 before any run.
- **A-01 (fixed):** a missing key is only `absent` on `ItemNotFoundException`; access or other read failures are `unreadable` with no `exists` claim. The child-specific **HKCU** `LocalDumps\powershell.exe` key is now inspected too.
- **A-02 (fixed):** the not-run list no longer calls the crash-report writer unimplemented; it names automatic on-crash capture, WER settings/control, export/consent and DD-22 export destinations, and states that the bounded writer/retention is implemented and covered by the app-core tests.
- **E. Judgment:**

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Configuration and boundary read/observed | **PASS_LIMITED** (observed: one correlated OS artifact, bounded scan of UTF-8/UTF-16LE, no leak) |
| WER artifact not produced / not correlated | **HOLD** (measured via `-SimulateWerHold`: overall HOLD, exit 2) |
| WER child skipped | **PASS_LIMITED with `wer_verified = false`** (measured) |
| Artifact unreadable | **NOT_VERIFIED** (proved by `-SimulateWerUnreadable`: `wer_boundary = NOT_VERIFIED`, overall HOLD, exit 2) |
| Synthetic secret leak | **FAIL** (proved by `-SimulateWerSecretLeak`: overall FAIL, exit 1) |
| Real Desktop crash verified | **NOT_RUN** (the Desktop was never crashed; no Desktop crash-report was produced or claimed) |

- **F. Negative tests (existing script, no new framework; measured):** `-SimulateWerSecretLeak` → FAIL (exit 1); `-SimulateWerUnreadable` → wer_boundary NOT_VERIFIED / overall HOLD (exit 2); `-SimulateWerHold` → HOLD (exit 2); `-SimulateUtf16Miss` → FAIL (exit 1, UTF-16 self-test); `-WerScanBytes 0` → refused (exit 2); `-SkipWerChildCrash` → NOT_RUN / overall PASS_LIMITED with `wer_verified=false` (exit 0); normal run → PASS_LIMITED (exit 0). The dump verification never folds into a full PASS.
- **Limits of this machine:** the agent process sandbox denies child writes outside the workspace, so evidence was written to a workspace-local `target/sec2-evidence` directory for these runs rather than the standard private evidence directory; the three induced dumps remain in the OS-managed `CrashDumps` area. The bounded scan covers only the first/last segment of the 27 MB dump, and OS-managed-area ownership/secrecy is read only for the listed attributes. **MP-SEC2 overall, WER control and Desktop crash-report automatic capture remain not claimed.**

### 19.127 decode-compare wall_ms: causal assertions replace machine-speed thresholds (2026-11-02)

- **Trigger:** the Gate on `7d667373` failed in two pre-existing `wall_ms < 1_100` timing-margin tests (`cancelled_candidate_does_not_wait_past_the_sample_bound`, `post_exit_harvest_does_not_inflate_wall_ms`) under load; the earlier record already named those as timing margins, not causal guarantees.
- **Causal assertions (no absolute machine-speed threshold):** the candidate itself now writes `candidate-start-at-ms` and `candidate-end-at-ms` epoch markers into the fixture base. The two post-exit tests assert
  `wall_ms <= (candidate_end − spawn_epoch) + 250 ms`, i.e. the recorded wall time is not longer than the candidate's own lifetime plus spawn/exit bookkeeping; a 2 s `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` added to `wall_ms` necessarily violates it. The cancelled test asserts
  `wall_ms <= cancellation_requested_at_ms + 250 ms` — the wall time cannot exceed the **observed cancellation request** by more than bookkeeping, which is machine-independent and fails if a post-exit grace is folded in. A **10 s sanity limit** remains and is labelled as such (not a timing threshold).
- **Negative proof (measured):** temporarily adding `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` (2 s) to `wall_ms` in the harness made all three tests **FAIL** — `post-exit harvest: wall 2102 ms exceeds the candidate lifetime (177 ms) + 250 ms`; `overrunning sample: wall 2102 ms exceeds the candidate lifetime (170 ms) + 250 ms`; `the recorded wall time 2301 ms exceeds the cancellation request 300 ms + 250 ms`. Restoring the harness returned all three to **PASS**; `harness.rs` has no diff.
- **Stability under load (measured):** `cargo test -p cos-desktop --test decode_compare_harness -- --test-threads=8` **10/10 runs green** (130 passed each). `cargo test --locked --workspace` with **5 parallel processes per round, 5 rounds**: the final matrix is **25/25 green** (3585 passed / 0 failed / 10 ignored per process, i.e. 5 × 717). An earlier matrix had one **unrelated transient** failure in `cos-client::recorded_context_missing_withholds_the_publication` (driver timeout under 5× parallel load, exit 101); it did not recur across the second 25-run matrix and is not one of the rewritten tests.
- **No WER change:** the WER boundary script and its evidence are untouched by this task.

### 19.128 decode-compare wall_ms: measured overhead replaces the fixed delta (2026-11-02)

- **Trigger:** the Gate on `140fd249` failed with `overrunning sample: wall 688 ms exceeds the candidate lifetime (192 ms) + 250 ms` — the fixed 250 ms bookkeeping delta cannot represent a loaded machine's real spawn/exit cost.
- **Calibration (same harness and helper, per test):** a new `exit-immediately` helper case ends as soon as it starts; each test runs it once and computes `overhead = calibration_wall_ms − candidate_lifetime` from the candidate's own epoch markers. The post-exit assertions are now
  `wall_ms <= measured_overhead + (candidate_end − candidate_start) + 250 ms`.
  The cancelled test uses a **kill-path calibration** (`cancellation_overhead_ms = cancelled_wall − cancellation_requested`) and asserts
  `wall_ms <= measured_kill_overhead + cancellation_requested_at_ms + 250 ms`.
  The 250 ms slack is only measurement fluctuation; an overhead above the **2 s detectable grace** makes the test **FAIL** (never skip), because a folded grace would be indistinguishable.
- **Measured overhead examples:** idle `6 ms (wall 7, lifetime 1)`, `6 ms (wall 8, lifetime 2)`, kill `1 ms (wall 301, requested 300)`; under a concurrent workspace suite the same calibration reported 6 ms / 6 ms / kill 1 ms, and the 5×5 parallel matrix below exercised the loaded case.
- **Negative proof (measured):** forcing `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` (2 s) into `wall_ms` makes the calibration report `overhead 2008 ms > 2000 ms` and all three tests **FAIL (exit 101)**; a test-side `wall_ms + 2000` reproduces the production assertion failure `wall 2107 ms exceeds measured overhead 6 ms + lifetime 52 ms + 250 ms`. Restoring both returns all three to **PASS**; `harness.rs` has no diff.
- **Stability (measured):** `decode_compare_harness --test-threads=8` **10/10 green** (130 passed each); `cargo test --locked --workspace` with **5 parallel processes per round, 5 rounds** = **25/25 green** (3585 passed / 0 failed / 10 ignored per process).
- **No WER change.** Test count remains 717 (assertions replaced, no new test cases).

### 19.129 decode-compare wall_ms: exit watcher freezes the measurement (2026-11-02)

- **Root cause found in code (not the grace constant):** `supervise` called `start_sample` **inside the supervision loop**; on the Gate host `Command::spawn` of the sampler (the harness test binary, ~35 MB) took ~2 s under load. The loop could not poll `child.try_wait()` during that call, so the candidate's exit (its markers show 51–52 ms) was observed ~2 s late and `wall_ms` was computed then. The numeric coincidence with `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` was incidental: the post-loop harvest already ran **after** `wall_ms`.
- **Fix:** a dedicated `ExitWatch` thread owns the child, polls `try_wait` every 2 ms and records the **exit `Instant`**; `wall_ms = exit_at − started`. Cancellation requests the kill through the watcher; the sampler join and the post-exit harvest run **after** the wall is frozen. The code comment states that `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` bounds harvest bookkeeping only, never the measurement.
- **Reproduction (fixed in the suite):** `a_slow_sampler_spawn_does_not_inflate_wall_ms` uses a test-only `Config.sample_spawn_delay` of 2.5 s to reproduce the Gate's process-creation cost; the recorded wall excludes it. A simulated 2.5 s block inside the supervision loop also leaves the test **PASS** with the watcher (it **FAILED** before the watcher).
- **Negative proof:** forcing `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE` (2 s) into `wall_ms` still makes all four wall tests **FAIL** — calibration reports 2006–2008 ms > the 2000 ms detectable grace, and a test-side `+2000` yields the exact assertion (`wall 2107 ms exceeds …`); restoring returns all four to PASS.
- **Stability (measured):** `decode_compare_harness --test-threads=8` **10/10 green** (131 passed each). The **5×5 parallel workspace matrix is not fully green**: 2 of 25 runs failed — `crash_report::a_linked_store_directory_is_refused` (junction creation unavailable under five simultaneous suites; the test fails closed by design, now with 10 retries) and `a_slow_sampler_spawn_does_not_inflate_wall_ms` (calibration preceded a load spike: wall 567 vs measured overhead 9 + lifetime 96 + 250). The three original Gate tests never failed in that matrix. Five concurrent full suites exceed the Gate condition (one suite plus machine load); this limitation is recorded rather than hidden.
- **Ancillary robustness (not WER):** the junction-retry count and the cos-client `wait_for` test deadline (5 s → 30 s, a test sanity bound) were widened after the 5×5 stress exposed resource-exhaustion failures. WER was not touched. Test count **718** (+1 reproduction test).

### 19.130 deadline enforcement and WER scan completeness (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** the hard deadline is now enforced by `ExitWatch` itself: the watcher kills the child when its deadline arrives even while `supervise` is blocked creating a sampler. `a_blocked_sampler_spawn_does_not_extend_the_deadline` (long candidate + 300 ms timeout + 2.5 s spawn delay) passes; disabling the watcher deadline makes it **FAIL** with `the candidate stopped at 2608 ms, past the 300 ms deadline + 250 ms slack`.
- **B-02 fixed:** the WER artifact scan uses `Read-ExactBytes` loops (first/last segment) and treats a short read as an incomplete scan (`readable = false`, `short_read = true`); `-SimulateWerShortRead` yields `wer_boundary = NOT_VERIFIED` / overall HOLD (exit 2).
- **A-01 fixed:** WER enumeration is bounded (`-MaxWerFiles 500`, `-MaxWerDepth 4`) with an explicit `capped` flag recorded in `enumeration_bounds`; `-SimulateWerEnumerationCap` yields NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD (exit 2).
- **A-02 fixed:** configuration completion is an independent condition (`config_read.verified`, `unreadable_keys`, `wer_config_verified`); any unreadable key makes the boundary NOT_VERIFIED even when artifacts were observed. `-SimulateWerConfigUnreadable` yields NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD (exit 2).
- **Measured matrix:** normal `PASS_LIMITED/0`; short-read, enumeration-cap and config-unreadable `NOT_VERIFIED/HOLD/2`; synthetic leak `FAIL/1`; skipped child `NOT_RUN` with `wer_verified=false` and overall `PASS_LIMITED/0`. Harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (132 tests each); workspace **719 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green.
- WER control/settings were not changed; no non-WER feature was added beyond the deadline fix.

### 19.131 normal-exit precedence and WER scan completeness (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** before any cap/deadline classification the supervisor re-checks `ExitWatch`: a normal exit recorded while the loop was blocked wins over `cancelled`/`timeout_fired`. `a_normal_exit_is_not_overwritten_by_a_late_deadline_check` (50 ms candidate, 300 ms timeout, 2.5 s sampler-spawn delay) asserts `Decoded`, `timeout_fired = false`, wall within the deadline; the deadline test (`a_blocked_sampler_spawn_does_not_extend_the_deadline`) still passes.
- **B-02 fixed:** `Find-TokenInBoundedFile` keeps `readable = false` when either segment short-reads, and `-SimulateWerShortRead` now requests one byte past EOF so a **genuine** short read occurs (no post-hoc override). The hardcoded `readable = true` was removed.
- **A-01 fixed:** the WER walk bounds **all visited entries including directories** (`-MaxWerFiles`), checks depth before descending, and never pushes a link/reparse point; `capped` is recorded when any bound is hit.
- **A-02 fixed:** unreadable WER roots are recorded per directory (`enumeration_bounds.unreadable_dirs`, `wer_enumeration_failed`) and force the boundary to **NOT_VERIFIED** without discarding the observed artifacts.
- **Measured WER matrix:** `NOT_RUN` when the child is skipped (`wer_verified=false`); `NOT_VERIFIED/HOLD` for enumeration cap, enumeration failure and config-unreadable (with the child run); synthetic-token leak `FAIL/1`; the normal run on this machine is **NOT_VERIFIED/HOLD** because the machine-wide WER roots (`ProgramData\...\WER`) are not readable to a standard user. In the short-read instrumented run the short read was recorded (`unreadable=1`) and the verdict was `FAIL` because the OS CrashDump genuinely contains the synthetic token (a true synthetic-secret leak in the OS-managed area, per the judgment table).
- **Gates:** harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (133 tests each); workspace **720 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green. WER settings were not changed.

### 19.132 watcher-side normal-exit precedence and bounded WER scanning (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed (watcher side):** `ExitWatch` now checks `try_wait()` **before** enforcing its deadline, and a kill request also checks for an already-finished child; only a real kill sets `killed_by_request`/`deadline_killed`. `a_late_watcher_poll_does_not_reclassify_a_normal_exit` (50 ms candidate, 300 ms timeout, 400 ms watcher polling delay) asserts `Decoded`/`timeout_fired=false`; `a_normal_exit_is_not_overwritten_by_a_late_deadline_check` and the deadline test remain green.
- **B-02 fixed:** the short-read simulation no longer allocates past the cap: it leaves one byte less in the stream (early EOF) while the 1 MiB bound is unchanged, and `readable = -not short_read` is preserved.
- **A-01 fixed:** WER enumeration streams `DirectoryInfo.EnumerateFileSystemInfos()` and stops at the entry cap instead of materialising the whole directory; directories count toward the bound, reparse points are never descended, and enumeration failures are recorded.
- **Measured WER matrix:** normal remains **NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD** (machine-wide `ProgramData\...\WER` is unreadable to a standard user); `-SkipWerChildCrash` → `NOT_RUN` / PASS_LIMITED; enumeration cap / configuration unreadable (with child) → NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD; synthetic-secret leak → FAIL. In the short-read run the short read is recorded (`unreadable=1`) and the verdict is FAIL because the OS CrashDump genuinely contains the synthetic token.
- **Gates:** harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (134 tests each); workspace **721 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green; WER settings unchanged.

### 19.133 deadline proof from the watcher instant and scoped WER short-read (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** deadline compliance is decided from the watcher's recorded exit instant, not from when the supervisor happened to look: `observed_late` is true only when the recorded observation is at/after the deadline, in which case the run is reported as a deadline overrun (`timeout_fired`, `Cancelled`) instead of `Decoded`. A candidate that exited before the deadline keeps `Decoded` even when the loop was blocked (50 ms exit / 300 ms deadline / 2.5 s spawn delay → PASS). New negative: 350 ms natural exit with a 300 ms deadline and a 400 ms watcher delay → `timeout_fired` + `Cancelled` (PASS).
- **B-02 fixed:** the short-read injection is scoped to WER artifact scans (`$script:shortReadInjection`), so the UTF-16LE self-test always runs under normal conditions; the stale post-scan `readable = false` override was removed. Measured: short-read run → `wer_boundary = NOT_VERIFIED` / overall **HOLD (exit 2)** with `utf16_selftest = PASS` (`matches_utf16le = 1`) and `unreadable = 1`.
- **A-01 fixed:** a single `$enumerated` counter limits every entry actually enumerated, including skipped reparse points, so many links can no longer bypass the bound; `capped = true` on reach.
- **Measured WER matrix:** normal remains **NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD** (machine-wide `ProgramData\...\WER` unreadable to a standard user); `-SkipWerChildCrash` → NOT_RUN / PASS_LIMITED; short-read and enumeration-cap → NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD; synthetic-secret leak → FAIL. The earlier short-read FAIL is explicitly **not** used as leak evidence: it was caused by the self-test corruption, now fixed.
- **Gates:** harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (135 tests each); workspace **722 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green; WER settings unchanged.

### 19.134 shared WER enumeration counter and honest late-observation state (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** `$enumerated` is now declared before the root loop, incremented for **every visited directory and every entry (including reparse points and skipped links)**, and the cap check uses it (plus `$visited`). `-MaxWerFiles 1` (a genuine enumeration bound, no simulation) yields `enumeration_capped = True` and `wer_boundary = NOT_VERIFIED` / overall **HOLD (exit 2)**.
- **B-02 fixed:** the late-observation path no longer fabricates a stop request: it sets `timeout_fired`/`cancelled` (non-success) but leaves `cancellation_requested_at_ms`/`cancellation_observed_ms` **None**, because no kill or stop request occurred. The 50 ms/350 ms negatives assert `cancellation_requested_at_ms.is_none()`.

The normal path varies between **NOT_VERIFIED/HOLD** (machine-wide `ProgramData\...\WER` unreadable) and **FAIL** when the bounded scan genuinely finds the synthetic token in the OS CrashDump; both are recorded as observed, never promoted to PASS.

### 19.135 sampler-timeout classification vs late-observation (2026-11-02)

- **Regression fixed:** the Gate failure `hanging_sampler_hits_the_sample_timeout` expected `sample_timeout` but received `no_sample`. The post-exit harvest killed an in-flight sampler without recording why; it now distinguishes the sampler's own per-sample timeout (a **real kill/stop request**, so `sample_timeout` is recorded) from the candidate's late-observation path (no stop request, so `cancellation_requested_at_ms` stays `None` and no `killed` is fabricated).
- **States kept separate:** candidate late observation → `timeout_fired`/`cancelled`, no cancellation timestamps, no kill; sampler timeout → `sample_timeout` with the real kill; deadline kill → `timeout_fired` with real cancellation timestamps.
- **Verified:** `hanging_sampler_hits_the_sample_timeout` 3/3; the 50 ms pre-deadline exit (`Decoded`), 350 ms post-deadline negative (non-success, no request time) and 300 ms deadline-kill test all PASS; harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (135 each); workspace **722 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green.

### 19.136 reparse-point accounting and real deadline-kill instants (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** `$enumerated++` now runs at the start of **every entry** in `foreach ($entry in $entries)` (before the reparse-point skip), so links count toward the bound; the cap check uses that counter. `-SelfTestWerReparseCap` builds a junction-only directory (3 junctions) and runs `Get-WerSnapshot` with `maxFiles = 1`; it reports `reparse_cap_selftest = PASS` (the cap fires). The default `-MaxWerFiles` was raised to 2000 so the real WER tree is bounded but still observable; `-MaxWerFiles 1` yields `capped = true` / NOT_VERIFIED / HOLD.
- **B-02 fixed:** `ExitWatch` records the **actual** `Instant` of the deadline kill request and of the confirmed exit; `supervise` derives `cancellation_requested_at_ms`/`cancellation_observed_ms` from them and leaves both `None` if the watcher could not record them. No estimated values are written. The three states stay separate: late observation (no request, timestamps None), sampler timeout (real kill → `sample_timeout`), deadline kill (real request/confirm instants).
- **Measured:** normal run → NOT_VERIFIED/HOLD with `correlated = 1`, `capped = false` (ProgramData WER subdirectories unreadable); reparse selftest PASS; `-MaxWerFiles 1` capped; harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (135 each); workspace **722 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green.

### 19.137 deadline-kill confirmation only on a successful wait (2026-11-02)

- **B-01 fixed:** `ExitWatch` records `deadline_kill_confirmed_at` **only when `child.wait()` succeeds**; a failed wait leaves it `None` (`cancellation_observed_ms = None`, exit status unknown) instead of publishing a latency. `child.kill()` errors are recorded as `kill_failed`; `deadline_killed` is set only when the kill was actually issued, and `supervise` reports the run as cancelled but **not killed** when the stop request failed (no successful-stop claim, no exit code from a kill).
- **Confirmed measurement:** `a_blocked_sampler_spawn_does_not_extend_the_deadline` now asserts a real request instant and a real confirmation latency; the late-observation paths still carry `None`.
- **Verified:** harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (135 tests each); workspace **722 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green.

### 19.138 ExitWatch as an explicit state machine (2026-11-02)

- **State enumeration:** `WatchState::{Running, Exited { at, status }, Unconfirmed { last_seen }}`. `Exited` is entered only when the exit is truly confirmed (a reaped status). `Unconfirmed` covers a failed kill, a failed/late confirmation, or a `try_wait` error; the watcher never performs an unbounded `wait()` and stops after the bounded confirmation window (`SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE`).
- **Effect on the recorded fields:**

| State | `wall_ms` | `killed` / `cancelled` | `cancellation_requested_at_ms` | `cancellation_observed_ms` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Running` | pending (no value) | — | — | — |
| `Exited` (normal) | `at − started` | not killed | `None` | `None` |
| `Exited` (deadline/request kill confirmed) | `at − started` | killed / cancelled | real request instant | real confirmation latency |
| `Unconfirmed` | **`None`** | **not killed**, cancelled | real request if one was issued | **`None`** |

- **Transitions tested (4):** normal exit → `Exited`; deadline kill + wait success → `Exited` with real request/confirm instants (`a_blocked_sampler_spawn_does_not_extend_the_deadline` asserts both); kill success + wait failure → `Unconfirmed` (`a_failed_wait_leaves_the_exit_unconfirmed`: `wall_ms = None`, `cancellation_observed_ms = None`); kill failure → `Unconfirmed`, no unbounded wait (`a_failed_kill_leaves_the_exit_unconfirmed`, finishes in < 1 s).
- **Gates:** harness `--test-threads=8` ×5 green (137 tests each); workspace **724 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**; fmt/clippy/build/dependency checker green.

#### 19.138.1 ExitWatch / cancel() contract (fixed before implementation)

| # | State / transition | `wall_ms` | `killed` | `cancelled` | `requested` | `observed` | Stop attempt | Bounded wait result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Running` | unset | false | false | `None` | `None` | none | still running | normal-exit tests (before exit) |
| 2 | `Exited` — natural exit (status reaped) | `at − started` | false | false | `None` | `None` | none | not needed | `post_exit_harvest_*`, `a_normal_exit_*` |
| 3 | `Exited` — kill issued and exit confirmed | `at − started` | true | true | real request instant | `confirm − request` | yes | confirmed | `a_blocked_sampler_spawn_*` |
| 4 | `Unconfirmed` — kill could not be issued | **`None`** | **false** | true | `None` | `None` | failed | failed | `a_failed_kill_*` |
| 5 | `Unconfirmed` — kill issued, exit not confirmed (incl. `try_wait` error) | **`None`** | **false** | true | real request instant | `None` | yes (kill then bounded confirm) | timeout/error | `a_failed_wait_*` |

- `cancel()` waits from a **fixed start instant** for at most `SAMPLE_EXIT_GRACE`; on timeout it returns `Unconfirmed` evidence (`observed = None`) and never infers an exit.
- `observed` is always `confirm_at − request_at`, never `now − started`.
- No state outside this table is implemented; an unconfirmed stop is never reported as `Exited` or `killed`.

### 19.140 MP-SEC2 limited: best-effort crash report on ordinary Rust panic (2026-11-02)

- **Implementation:** `app_core::panic_report::install(version)` registers one hook at the very start of `main` (inside `install`, `INSTALLED`/`IN_HOOK` atomics make later installs and re-entrant panics no-ops). `set_hook` replaces the installed hook directly — `take_hook` is not used, so the default payload-printing hook is never briefly active — and the replaced hook is never called, so the payload/backtrace print path is gone. The hook calls the existing `CrashReportStore::open_default()` and `save()` with `CrashReportInput { desktop_version, category: Unknown, diagnostics: None }`; no payload, backtrace, error text, path or credential is read. The body uses only `Result`-returning operations, so ordinary I/O failures cannot start a second panic; the `catch_unwind` guard covers ordinary unwinding only and is **not** a second-panic defence (Rust aborts when a panic hook panics), which is not claimed. Failures leave the original exit status intact.
- **Diagnostics:** `diagnostics: None` is explicit — the ring is not reachable from the panic path without a blocking lock, and the report renders "the diagnostic ring was not read".
- **Tests (6):** `panic_report_helper_modes` plus `a_panic_writes_one_report_without_the_payload`, `a_normal_exit_writes_no_report`, `a_double_install_still_writes_one_report`, `a_blocked_store_does_not_recurse_or_change_the_exit`, `the_existing_three_report_limit_is_kept` (isolated child `LOCALAPPDATA`; synthetic secret never reaches the file **or the child's stderr**, and the default backtrace hint is absent; retention 3 kept and readable after restart).
- **Reached / not reached:** ordinary Rust panic capture = REACHED (limited); normal exit = no report REACHED; OS forced termination, `FailFast` and WER exceptions = NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT CLAIMED; WER settings and diagnostic-ring persistence were not changed. **MP-SEC2 overall remains HOLD.**
- **Gates:** fmt clean, clippy 0, workspace **733 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored** (38 binaries), build and dependency checker OK.

### 19.141 MP-FLOW2 Stage C cache-miss first frame, re-measured with per-sample evidence (2026-11-02)

- **Conditions:** release, rustc/cargo `1.98.1`, Windows x64, 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges (100 layers x 100 nodes), `MAX_DIAGRAM_NODES = 120`, single-entry `MatchCache`, 3 warmups, **21 measured iterations**, miss and hit **interleaved** (even iterations `replace → hit → clear`, odd `clear → hit → replace`). Timed interval = `get_or_build` + diagram construction only; `clear()` and prefill are outside the timer. median = middle (mean of the two middles for an even count); p95 = nearest-rank `ceil(n*0.95)-1`; max = largest. **Raw samples (63 lines) are printed by the test and were retained in `target/flow2-raw.log`; they are not committed because `target/` is excluded.**
- **Series (microseconds, n=21):**

| series | median | p95 | max | match median/p95 | diagram median/p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| `miss_clear` (rebuild after `clear()`) | 13,923 | 14,471 | 14,565 | 10,940 / 11,365 | 3,001 / 3,106 |
| `miss_replace` (existing entry replaced by a new `AdmissionKey`) | 15,130 | 16,573 | 17,438 | 12,063 / 13,545 | 3,083 / 3,222 |
| `hit` (cache hit) | 2,065 | 2,665 | 2,776 | 0 / 0 | 2,065 / 2,664 |

- **Correction to the earlier single-block run:** the previous 13.65 ms figure was the post-`clear()` rebuild measured as a block. The `miss_replace` series replaces an existing entry with a **synthetic new `query` key over the same rows**, so it measures entry replacement at the same data volume - not a real search-result change or a whole Runtime projection update. In that condition it costs **~1.2 ms more than the clear path (p95 +2.1 ms)** because the old entry is discarded inside the timed region. **Total CPU load of a real key change in production is NOT_MEASURED.**
- **Samples retained:** the 63 per-iteration samples are reproduced verbatim below (§19.141.1); the reported median/p95/max were re-computed from them and match. `docs/development/evidence/` is git-ignored by policy, so the samples live in this tracked section instead.
- **Judgement (CPU only; paint/GPU/Present NOT_MEASURED):** `hit` fits both the 60 Hz budget and the 8.33 ms UI target. `miss_clear` fits the 60 Hz budget (p95 14.47 ms, ~2.2 ms margin) but not the 8.33 ms target. `miss_replace` reaches **p95 16.57 ms against the 16.67 ms budget** - essentially no margin - so **first-frame improvement is required before an entry-replacing key change can be called safe at 60 Hz**; whether a real Runtime projection update also fits is NOT_MEASURED. The stateful `match` set construction (12.06 ms median) remains the dominant cost; the layer recomputation measured earlier at ~4.03 ms is a separate, avoidable cost when only `revision` changes.
- **Key invalidation and equivalence:** each of `session_generation`, `publication_version`, `epoch`, `revision`, `query` changed alone produces a miss and an unchanged key still hits (5/5). miss/hit/reference diagrams agree structurally and share the deterministic checksum `0xd3e2fdd3e8aa45f2`. Authorization-loss reuse is covered by the existing `clear()` contract test; no new Runtime projection path was exercised.
- **Not measured / not claimed:** GPUI paint, submit, GPU and Present; the real-world miss frequency; Runtime projected graphs. MP-FLOW2 overall remains incomplete. No new cache was implemented and no production code path was changed by this measurement slice.

### 19.143 MP-FLOW2 Stage C: BTreeSet → HashSet A/B (2026-11-02)

- **Baseline (§19.141.1, committed BTreeSet, same 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges, release, warmup 3, 21 iterations):** miss_replace 15,130 / 16,573 / 17,438 µs; miss_clear 13,923 / 14,471 / 14,565 µs; hit 2,065 / 2,665 / 2,776 µs. The 63 baseline samples stay recorded there and are not rewritten.
- **Candidate:** `Matched.nodes` / `Matched.edges` use `std::collections::HashSet`; the production builder allocates `HashSet::with_capacity(rows.nodes.len() / rows.edges.len())` and extends once; `diagram` takes `&HashSet`; `AdmissionKey`, `MatchCache` (single entry, five-component invalidation, `clear()`), `Rows`, `Layers` and GPU drawing are unchanged.
- **A/B scope, stated precisely:** the A/B series measures a **representative HashSet build** (`.collect()`), while production builds with `HashSet::with_capacity` + one `extend`; the two are not the same code. The product-path figures below come from the product cache in the same run, but the **BTreeSet product path was not measured in that run**, so the 15,130 → 12,593 µs change is a **cross-run reference, not a same-run A/B**. Adoption rests on the large **same-run** build and probe differences, which are measured under identical conditions.
- **A/B (same run, same rows/graph refs, alternating order, release):**

| series (n=21) | median | p95 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BTreeSet build | 9,994 µs | 11,208 µs | 11,433 µs |
| HashSet build | 7,749 µs | 8,065 µs | 8,200 µs |
| BTreeSet probe (all 29,800 memberships) | 16,791 µs | 17,569 µs | 17,866 µs |
| HashSet probe | 9,501 µs | 9,995 µs | 10,153 µs |
| product miss_clear total | 10,195 µs | 11,483 µs | 11,755 µs |
| product miss_replace total | 12,593 µs | 13,410 µs | 14,174 µs |
| product hit total | 1,791 µs | 2,040 µs | 2,602 µs |

  Build median improves by **2,245 µs (22.5%)** and probe median by **7,290 µs** in the same run; product `miss_replace` falls from the committed 15,130 µs baseline to 12,593 µs, and `hit` does not regress (2,065 → 1,791 µs; diagram-dominated).
- **Correctness:** btree/hash sets are equal element-wise; **three independently built diagrams** - from the BTreeSet-derived sets, from the HashSet-derived `hash_ref`, and the cached reference - are structurally identical, and the deterministic diagram checksum is asserted equal across all three paths and printed by the test. All existing flow tests pass (deterministic order/diagram, cap 120, skipped count, key invalidation 5/5, `clear()` rebuild, single-entry bound).
- **Decision: ADOPT** (all E conditions met). MP-FLOW2 overall, paint/GPU/Present and real Runtime projection graphs remain unfinished.

### 19.144 MP-FLOW2 revision change vs query-only: CPU decomposition (2026-11-02)

> Superseded by the corrected-condition re-measurement in §19.145: the query-only series here also changed `publication_version` and the query string, so its difference from the revision series is not attributable to a revision change. The values below stay as a conditional observation only.

- **Contract (unchanged):** `RevisionKey` (`GraphRef + source_revision`) keys the Layers cache; the match cache is keyed by the five-component `AdmissionKey` (revision, epoch, publication version, session generation, query). A revision change invalidates both; a query-only change invalidates only the match set (and re-derives Rows), while Layers stay valid.
- **Conditions (release, warmup 3, 21 iterations, alternating; same 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges):** query-only = same `GraphRef` + new `query`; revision = new `GraphRef` version/digest + `source_revision = 2` with unchanged node/edge topology. These are synthetic identifier mutations, not real Runtime updates.
- **Results (median / p95 / max, µs):**

| condition | rows (background) | layers (display) | match set (display) | diagram (display) | display total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| query-only | 12,789 / 16,165 / 20,718 | 0 (cached reuse) | 3,158 / 4,709 / 7,637 | 5,108 / 6,412 / 6,848 | 7,605 / 11,121 / 13,708 |
| revision | 825 / 1,168 / 1,526 | 5,814 / 8,316 / 8,448 | 9,220 / 12,664 / 13,024 | 2,970 / 3,819 / 3,910 | 18,172 / 24,404 / 24,607 |

  Rows run in the background class and are not summed with display-side values into a frame latency. Layers recompute is 32% of the revision display total; match-set rebuild is 51%.
- **Correctness:** Layers depth/cyclic equal to the pre-change graph; Diagram has 120 nodes, `truncated = true`, `skipped_edges = 19,760`; node/edge identities, order and depths unchanged; match sets for the new revision carry only the new `GraphRef` (no cross-revision reuse). Existing deterministic/key/clear tests pass.
- **Judgment:** after HashSet, a revision-change display-side CPU total is **~18.2 ms median (p95 24.4 ms)**, above the 60 Hz CPU budget (16.67 ms); query-only is ~7.6 ms. The remaining cost is the match-set rebuild (9.2 ms) plus Layers recompute (5.8 ms). Additional optimization (for example incremental Layers or not rebuilding the full match set) is **not implemented in this slice**; the next measurement should be paint/GPU/present, real Runtime revision frequency, and a Layers-recompute decomposition.

### 19.145 MP-FLOW2 revision change: corrected conditions (2026-11-02)

> Superseded by §19.146: this run still primed the query-only cache entry from the revision key, so three key components changed. The values below stay as a conditional observation only.

- **Corrections from review:** §19.144's query-only condition also changed `publication_version` and reduced the match-set cardinality; it is retained there only as a **conditional observation** and is not used for decisions. In this section the query-only key keeps the **same revision and publication version** and changes **only `query`** (`""` → whitespace-only, which trims to the empty filter); the revision key fixes `query = ""` and changes **only `GraphRef`/`source_revision` and `publication_version`**.
- **Terminology (A-01):** all values are `Instant::elapsed()` **sequential elapsed time**, not thread CPU time. Rows and the display-side steps run sequentially inside the test. The display total **excludes paint, GPU submission, Present and drawable element construction**, and is not a frame latency; the comparison with 16.67 ms is a **reference only**, not proof of a frame-budget overrun.
- **Asserted conditions:** query-only admits the same 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges and the same match-set cardinality; revision-change Layers depth/cyclic equal; the revision Diagram equals the reference Diagram computed from the new `GraphRef` (node/edge identities, order, depths), `nodes.len() == 120`, `truncated`, `edges + skipped_edges == 19,800`, and a deterministic checksum on every iteration.
- **Results (release, warmup 3, 21 iterations, alternating; median / p95 / max, µs):**

| condition | rows (background) | layers (display) | match set (display) | diagram (display) | display total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| query-only (only `query` changes) | 626 / 924 / 1,309 | 0 (cached) | 12,400 / 14,612 / 16,125 | 2,939 / 3,748 / 3,899 | 15,475 / 17,549 / 20,024 |
| revision (only `GraphRef`/revision + publication version change) | 716 / 1,138 / 1,303 | 6,369 / 7,336 / 7,520 | 12,382 / 13,646 / 13,962 | 2,990 / 3,970 / 4,001 | 21,900 / 23,426 / 24,224 |

  With the same match-set cardinality, the revision-specific difference is the **Layers recompute (~6.4 ms median)**; match-set rebuild is ~12.4 ms in both conditions. No optimization is implemented in this slice.

### 19.147 MP-FLOW2 Layers recompute: seven-phase decomposition (2026-11-02)

- **Implementation:** `layers()` delegates to `layers_inner(graph, #[cfg(test)] phases)`; the product call passes nothing. Under `#[cfg(test)]` the path explicitly `drop`s the index map and adjacency as **P7 (deallocation)** before returning, and `layers_phased()` returns the phases, the **outer elapsed** `outer_total_us`, and the per-iteration phase sum. **outer_total is not the sum of phases.**
- **Phases:** P1 NodeId→index HashMap; P2 successors adjacency; P3 iterative Tarjan SCC; P4 condensation DAG + indegree; P5 Kahn depth; P6 cyclic/depth array; P7 explicit deallocation. No independent sort exists.
- **Conditions:** release, 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges synthetic DAG, warmup 3, 21 iterations; sequential elapsed µs (`Instant::elapsed`), not CPU time.
- **Results (median / p95 / max, µs; share is of the outer median):**

| phase | median | p95 | max | share of outer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 index | 973 | 1367 | 1488 | 17.0% |
| P2 successors | 2862 | 3527 | 3623 | 49.9% |
| P3 Tarjan | 366 | 456 | 501 | 6.4% |
| P4 condense | 480 | 551 | 683 | 8.4% |
| P5 Kahn | 98 | 108 | 109 | 1.7% |
| P6 depth | 12 | 15 | 16 | 0.2% |
| P7 deallocation (explicit drop) | 552 | 666 | 691 | 9.6% |
| phase sum (per iteration) | 5541 | 6026 | 6643 | — |
| **unattributed (outer − sum)** | **197** | **247** | **280** | 3.4% |
| **outer_total_us** | **5739** | **6227** | **6836** | 100% |

  The explicit P7 drop accounts for the previously unexplained cost (552 µs median). The residual ~197 µs is the measured boundary between `outer` and the sum (timer calls and unsampled transition work), recorded as unattributed rather than assumed to be overhead. Percentages use the outer median as denominator. They also do not sum to 100 because each phase median is computed independently, so the individual medians need not occur in the same iteration; compare shares as orientation only, and read the per-iteration samples for attribution.
- **Difference from §19.146:** §19.146 measured un-instrumented `layers()` (median 5,929 µs) in the revision condition; here the phased path with outer total measures 5739 µs median. The ranges overlap; the phased run is not a product-cost claim.
- **Candidates (hypotheses only, not verified by this measurement; no adoption or implementation):**
  (1) P2 successors → multi-pass CSR (count out-degree, then fill). The 1–2 ms saving is an **unverified hypothesis**; a real CSR needs several passes, and **adjacency order must be preserved** because node/edge order affects deterministic depth/Diagram results. Correctness risk: order and duplicate edges must stay identical.
  (2) P1 index → pre-size HashMap with node count (or a dense identity pass). The 0.2–0.4 ms saving is an **unverified hypothesis**; identity checks and collision behavior must not change.
- **Limits:** paint/GPU/Present not measured; no Stage A–C experiment, no numeric gate, no optimization implemented. MP-FLOW2 remains incomplete.
- **Raw samples (21 iterations; outer totals and per-phase values):**

### 19.148 MP-FLOW2 P2 successors: P2a/P2b split (2026-11-02)

- **Implementation:** only `#[cfg(test)]` timing points were added to `layers_inner`, and every timer, including the clock creation, is conditional on a phase array being supplied, so the non-instrumented path takes no timestamps at all; P1–P7 definitions are unchanged. P2 is the whole successors pass; **P2a** is the outer `vec![Vec::new(); count]` initialisation and **P2b** is the compound edge pass (NodeId→index lookups, `push`, inner Vec growth). P2 overall is computed as P2a+P2b (asserted equal per iteration); no per-edge timers and no duplicated algorithm.
- **Conditions:** release, 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges synthetic DAG, warmup 3, 21 iterations, `Instant::elapsed()` sequential time. `phase_sum` is P1..P7 only; P2a/P2b are subdivisions and are not added again. `outer_total − phase_sum` is recorded as unattributed.
- **Results (median / p95 / max, µs; share of outer median):**

| phase | median | p95 | max | share of outer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 index | 1041 | 1208 | 1283 | 17.9% |
| P2 all | 2932 | 3174 | 3327 | 50.3% |
| **P2a outer init** | **12** | **38** | **43** | 0.2% |
| **P2b edge pass (compound)** | **2895** | **3164** | **3317** | 49.7% |
| P3 Tarjan | 354 | 472 | 625 | 6.1% |
| P4 condense | 471 | 570 | 581 | 8.1% |
| P5 Kahn | 99 | 124 | 134 | 1.7% |
| P6 depth | 14 | 23 | 30 | 0.2% |
| P7 deallocation | 563 | 729 | 913 | 9.7% |
| phase sum (P1..P7) | 5608 | 5845 | 6041 | — |
| unattributed (outer − sum) | 198 | 288 | 409 | 3.4% |
| outer_total | 5828 | 6087 | 6238 | 100% |

  P2a is negligible (12 µs); **P2b is the dominant part of P2** (2,895 of 2,932 µs). P2b is a compound step, so its cost is not attributed separately to HashMap lookup or Vec growth.
- **Consistency:** per iteration P2a+P2b == P2 (asserted); `phase_sum` excludes the P2a/P2b split and does not double count; unattributed remains ~198 µs.
- **Correctness:** phased and unphased results are identical every iteration; depths equal the independent Kahn reference; 10,000 nodes / 19,800 edges; the existing Diagram/checksum assertions remain unchanged. No new tests were added.
- **Hypothesis re-evaluation (no speed estimate, no adoption):** the outer vector initialisation (P2a) is ~0.2% of the outer time, so pre-sizing *that* allocation is not a meaningful lever. Pre-sizing the **inner per-node Vec capacities** and the **P1 index map** act on different code (P2b growth and P1 respectively) and their effect is **NOT MEASURED** by this slice - the P2b figure is a compound cost and cannot be split that way. CSR would restructure the P2b edge pass, which is where the time is; any benefit is a **hypothesis** needing its own measurement, and it must preserve adjacency order (determinism). No absolute comparison with §19.147 is interpreted as a speed change.
- **Limits:** paint/GPU/Present not measured; no Stage A–C experiment, no numeric gate, no optimization implemented. MP-FLOW2 remains incomplete.
- **Raw samples (21 iterations; outer, P2 split, phase sum, unattributed):**
